items.desc: Overview We are seeking a Research Fellow to join LungSight, a multidisciplinary project developing low-cost, non-invasive audio-visual AI for earlier identification of chronic lung disease. The project aims to support a shift from reactive, clinic-based diagnosis towards proactive home screening using everyday devices such as smartphones, tablets and home computers. Based in the School of Engineering at the University of Southampton, you will lead the research engineering clinically informed acoustic features for fine-tuning machine learning models of respiratory health. You will work with large-scale real-world recordings of speech, breathing and cough, developing acoustic features that are robust to noise, demographic variation and different recording environments, predictive of early-stage chronic respiratory conditions and explainable in terms of the natural history of disease. You will also contribute to development of machine learning models and to the integration of audio with visual and clinical information. LungSight is a multi-university collaboration also involving Manchester Metropolitan University, the University of Cambridge, the University of Leicester, the University of Leeds, and the University of Sheffield alongside NHS and third-sector partners. This post will work particularly closely with a complementary PDRA at the University of Sheffield, whose research will focus more strongly on development of machine learning models while the Southampton post has a stronger focus on acoustic features and clinical knowledge mapping. The role offers opportunities for high-quality publications, open research outputs, clinical and stakeholder engagement, and career development at the interface of AI and healthcare. Main Duties And Responsibilities Develop and evaluate acoustic feature sets predictive of respiratory health using speech, breathing and cough recordings. Curate, pre-process and analyse large-scale real-world audio datasets, including sensitive healthcare and helpline recordings processed within appropriate secure data environments. Fine-tune and validate models on labelled respiratory datasets and clinically relevant downstream tasks, assessing accuracy, generalisability and clinical utility. Investigate potential confounding factors, demographic bias, background-noise effects and effects of recording environment, to support feature robustness and equitable model performance. Contribute to development of self-supervised models, working closely with the Sheffield PDRA who will lead complementary machine learning research; investigate how engineered physiological features can be combined with learned representations from the Sheffield machine-learning work. Collaborate with project researchers to develop multimodal approaches combining acoustic, visual and clinical information for respiratory disease screening. Work closely with researchers across the LungSight consortium, including Manchester Metropolitan Sheffield, Cambridge, Leicester and Leeds Universities, as well as clinical, NHS, patient/public and third-sector partners; participate in project meetings, joint research activities and dissemination. Lead and contribute to high-quality research publications and presentations, support project reporting, and contribute to the supervision and development of students where appropriate. You should hold hold a PhD (or equivalent research experience) in Computer Science, Electronic Engineering, Speech/Audio Processing, Machine Learning, Biomedical Engineering or a closely related discipline, with research experience in speech, audio, acoustic signal processing or closely related time-series analysis. Working At The University Of Southampton Check out the staff benefits and why you should join us at The University of Southampton.

With strong
items.desc: Le descriptif de l’offre ci-dessous est en Anglais Contrat renouvelable : Oui Niveau de diplôme exigé : Thèse ou équivalent Fonction : Ingénieur scientifique contractuel Niveau d'expérience souhaité : Jeune diplômé A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle Inria is the French National Institute for Research in Digital Science, of which the Inria Côte d'Azur University Center is a part. With strong expertise in computer science and applied mathematics, the research projects of the Inria Côte d'Azur University Center cover all aspects of digital science and technology and generate innovation. Based mainly in Sophia Antipolis, but also in Nice and Montpellier, it brings together 47 research teams and nine support services. It is active in the fields of artificial intelligence, data science, IT system security, robotics, network engineering, natural risk prevention, ecological transition, digital biology, computational neuroscience, health data, and more. The Inria Center at Université Côte d'Azur is a major player in terms of scientific excellence, thanks to the results it has achieved and its collaborations at both European and international level. Contexte et atouts du poste We are recruiting a researche engineer to develop machine-learning methods for analyzing high-dimensional, multimodal medical imaging data. The project focuses on whole-body positron emission tomography combined with computed tomography (PET/CT) in metastatic lung cancer. The goal is to jointly leverage metabolic and anatomical imaging information to characterize disease and improve the prediction of survival outcomes. The work will be conducted in a clinical and translational setting, in collaboration with specialists in medical imaging, oncology, and biostatistics. Mission confiée The engineer will: Design and evaluate survival analysis methods suited to censored data and clinical cohorts. Develop learned representations from PET and CT images, both separately and jointly. Investigate strategies for analyzing whole-body scans, including the detection and characterization ofmultiple lesions. Integrate clinical, biological, or treatment-related variables with imaging representations, when available. Assess model robustness, generalizability, and calibration across data from different centers or imagingsystems. Lesion segmentation and detection: Automatic or semi-supervised segmentation, detection of tumor foci,and extraction of lesion-level features. Self-supervised and contrastive learning: Pretraining on unlabeled scans, learning robust representations,and reducing reliance on manual annotations. Weakly supervised and multiple-instance learning: Representing a scan as a set of regions or lesionswhen only patient-level annotations are available. Deep learning–based survival models: Risk models, survival functions, and methods that account forcensoring, potentially conditioned on multimodal features. Longitudinal data: Incorporating repeated scans and changes in tumor burden over time. Robustness and generalizability: Data harmonization, domain adaptation, and assessment of differencesrelated to centers, scanners, and acquisition protocols. Interpretability and uncertainty: Identifying regions or lesions associated with predictions, analyzinguncertainty, and calibrating estimated risks. Experience in deep learning and medical image analysis, ideally involving 3D or multimodal data. Knowledge of survival analysis and censored data, or a strong motivation to develop expertise in theseareas. Proficiency in Python and a deep-learning framework such as PyTorch. items.desc: About Vibraint Vibraint is a TechBio company working with neuroscientists in academia, biotech and pharma to understand the brain in health and disease. Modern brain imaging can capture every cell in a whole mouse brain, but turning those complex datasets into reliable answers, and linking them to other experiments, is still slow and fragmented. Our aim is to close that gap and help accelerate the search for treatments for brain disorders. LS-Journey™ is our whole-brain light sheet imaging and analysis service. It covers brains imaged in our own lab as well as data from customers’ microscopes. CNS-Voyager™ is our cloud-based virtual brain platform. There, extracted signals from whole brain 3D microscopy meet gene expression profiles and other reference data, so patterns can be explored across experiments and techniques. This is what we call integrative spatial biology: layering molecular, functional, and anatomical information to build a richer picture of brain biology. Position We are looking for a skilled Computational Scientist to become our in-house expert in AI, computer vision and spatial omics, and to help build the software that connects all of this. You will develop AI models and robust, automated pipelines for up to terabyte-scale 3D brain data, running both locally and in the cloud. You will also work on methods that bridge light sheet imaging with molecular data. Roughly half of your time will go to analysing customer studies and half to building the tools, models and infrastructure behind our platforms. Key responsibilities Running and improving analysis pipelines for customer studies, from raw light sheet data to quality-controlled, biologically interpretable results. Developing and validating deep learning models for 3D segmentation, classification, registration and feature extraction. Taking technical ownership of a modular, well-tested and documented codebase that runs both locally and, in the cloud, and establishing good software development practices. Building infrastructure for training, tracking, and monitoring AI models and their data. Adapting models and algorithms to accommodate light sheet data from external customers’ microscopes, handling differences in acquisition, labelling and data quality. Building easy-to-use tools for training data generation, model and parameter optimization, automated quality control of samples, scans and analytical steps. Contributing to analytics and multimodal data integration in CNS-Voyager™. Developing methods that bridge light sheet imaging and spatial omics, including predictive models linking brain imaging and gene expression. Advising the team on AI, mathematical and statistical approaches, and contributing to our research roadmap. Key competencies a nd qualifications You combine scientific curiosity with strong computational and engineering skills. You are comfortable translating scientific questions into computational problems and developing robust software solutions to address them. You care about clean architecture as much as about high-quality results, and you would rather build a tool once than repeat the same analysis a thousand times. You communicate clearly with people from very different backgrounds, and you enjoy the pace and variety of a small, growing company. Required: An MSc or PhD in computer science, computational biology, biomedical engineering, applied mathematics, physics or a related quantitative field. At least 2 years of relevant research or professional experience developing computational methods, software, or machine learning models. This may include experience gained during a PhD, postdoctoral research, or equivalent industry experience. Strong Python software engineering skills, including modular design, testing, version control, performance optimization, and documentation. Proven experience building automated, scalable pipelines for multidimensional image data, including segmentation, registration and quantitative feature extraction. Proven experience independently developing, training, and validating machine learning and deep learning models (e.g. using PyTorch), with a solid understanding of neural network architectures, optimization methods, and their mathematical foundations. Experience adapting and improving existing architectures as well as developing new computational approaches. Solid knowledge of statistics and experimental design in biological research. items.desc: About The Company Models are what they eat. But a large portion of training compute is wasted training on data that are already learned, irrelevant, or even harmful, leading to worse models that cost more to train and deploy. At DatologyAI, we’ve built a state of the art data curation suite to automatically curate and optimize petabytes of data to create the best possible training data for your models. Training on curated data can dramatically reduce training time and cost ( 7-40x faster training depending on the use case), dramatically increase model performance as if you had trained on >10x more raw data without increasing the cost of training, and allow smaller models with fewer than half the parameters to outperform larger models despite using far less compute at inference time, substantially reducing the cost of deployment. For more details, check out our recent research on synthetic data scaling (BeyondWeb) and pretraining with domain-specific data (The Finetuner’s Fallacy). We raised a total of $57.5M in two rounds, a Seed and Series A. Our investors include Felicis Ventures, Radical Ventures, Amplify Partners, Microsoft, Amazon, and AI visionaries like Geoff Hinton, Yann LeCun, Jeff Dean, and many others who deeply understand the importance and difficulty of identifying and optimizing the best possible training data for models. Our team has pioneered this frontier research area and has the deep expertise on both data research and data engineering necessary to solve this incredibly challenging problem and make data curation easy for anyone who wants to train their own model on their own data. This is a hybrid role based in London, UK. Once our office is up and running, the team will work on-site 4 days a week. About The Role We're looking for a Research Scientist to investigate how intervening on training data can improve the quality and shape the behavior of deep learning models. You'll source and implement ideas from the literature, conduct research grounded in real customer needs, and collaborate closely with engineers and product teams to turn findings into tangible impact. This role requires strong scientific judgment, fluency with the deep learning literature, and the drive to work autonomously in a fast-moving startup environment. What You'll Work On The research literature is vast, rife with ambiguity, and constantly evolving. You'll source, vet, implement, and improve promising ideas from the literature and your own thinking. Our research is guided by concrete customer needs and product outcomes, not conference benchmarks. You'll have clear context on why your work matters and who it serves. How You'll Work We believe researchers do their best work with autonomy. You'll have the freedom to pursue problems in the way that works best for you, with the resources and context to back it up. We expect Research Scientists to collaborate closely with engineers, talk to customers, and shape the product vision. About You 3+ years of deep learning research experience Strong fundamentals in deep learning Practical experience and/or publications in one or more of the following areas: Data pruning and curation Curriculum learning Synthetic data generation Dataset distillation Effects of training data on model behavior Embedding models and semantic search Training large vision (including video), language, or multimodal models Efficient ML Enough software engineering and PyTorch experience (or willingness to learn) to run large-scale experiments and build production prototypes A demonstrated track record in deep learning research, whether through papers, tools, or other artifacts Nice To Have Experience with distributed data processing tools like Spark or Snowflake Experience building and shipping ML products Candidates do not need a PhD or extensive publications. Some of the best researchers we've worked with have no formal training in machine learning, and obtained all of their experience working in industry and building products. We believe adaptability, combined with exceptional communication and collaboration skills, are the most important ingredients for successful research in a startup environment. Compensation £140,000 to £355,000 + Offers Equity This is a position with Datology UK Limited, which controls the hiring and management of this position. Total compensation includes competitive salary, generous equity and benefits.

 Research Intern – Scientific Machine Learning for Physics and Simulation 
 Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. Improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you? 
 Transform the everyday with us! 
 You will join the Physics x AI research lab within Siemens’ Data and Artificial Intelligence organization — our central research hub for artificial intelligence — for a Spring 2027 internship. 
 We are looking for a Research Intern in Scientific Machine Learning for Physics and Simulation. This position will be remote. 
 You’ll make an impact by: 
 • Developing and evaluating neural surrogate models that predict physical fields and engineering quantities on complex geometries. 
 • Incorporating physical laws, boundary conditions, and engineering knowledge into artificial intelligence models. 
 • Studying model accuracy and generalization across geometries, meshes, and operating conditions. 
 • Designing experiments with appropriate baselines, ablation studies, and reproducible evaluation. 
 • Implementing research prototypes, data pipelines, and GPU training workflows, and validating predictions together with simulation experts. 
 • Communicating findings through technical reports, presentations, and scientific papers. 
 You’ll win us over by having the following qualifications: 
 Basic Qualifications: 
 Currently enrolled as a PhD student in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, or a related field.
 Research experience in machine learning and deep learning, including developing and evaluating new methods.
 Hands-on experience developing and training neural networks in Python with PyTorch or a comparable deep-learning framework, including designing experiments and comparing models against baselines.
 A sound foundation in linear algebra, optimization, probability, and numerical computation.
 A background in physics, engineering, or physical modeling, with the ability to learn new scientific concepts with guidance from domain experts, and clear written and verbal communication skills.
 Minimal travel required (less than 10%).
 Proficient in English both written and verbal
 Legally authorized to work in the United States on a continual and permanent basis without company sponsorship.
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Publications at leading artificial intelligence conferences (for example, NeurIPS, ICML, or ICLR), or in relevant scientific journals.
 Surrogate modeling, neural operators, geometry-aware machine learning, or graph neural networks for meshes, point clouds, or CAD geometry.
 Physics-informed machine learning, differentiable simulation, uncertainty quantification, or learning from limited simulation data.
 Scientific foundation models, multimodal learning, or generative artificial intelligence (pretraining, fine-tuning, diffusion, or flow-based models) for physical prediction, geometry generation, or inverse design.
 Agentic artificial intelligence for tool use and simulation workflows, or reinforcement learning for engineering design, optimization, or control.
 Computational fluid dynamics, heat transfer, numerical PDE methods, or multiphysics modeling (for example, Simcenter STAR-CCM+, OpenFOAM, or NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo), and GPU or distributed computing for large simulation datasets.

 We are a global technology company focused on industry, infrastructure, transport, and healthcare. From more resource-efficient factories, resilient supply chains, and smarter buildings and grids, to sustainable transportation as well as advanced healthcare, we create technology with purpose adding real value for customers.

 We value your unique identity and perspective. We welcome you to bring your authentic self and transform the everyday with us. …

items.desc: At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound. Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation. Description Job Description The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices for applications such as context understanding, dynamic awareness, augmented hearing and ones we haven’t yet imagined. You will work with experts in ML, DSP, software engineering, and psychoacoustics to prototype and implement new algorithms. You will develop audio understanding algorithms that enable devices to recognize what is happening in the world around them. Areas of interest include sound event detection and localization (SELD), acoustic scene understanding, unusual or anomalous sound detection, and multimodal context understanding from audio, video, and motion sensors. Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next. Responsibilities Research, prototype, train, and evaluate novel audio understanding models, from early experiments through real-time deployment on devices. Develop robust methods for sound event detection/localization, acoustic anomaly detection, and context-aware audio interpretation. Explore multimodal approaches that combine microphone signals with video, IMU, or other sensor data when useful. Build and curate datasets and data piplines, evaluation protocols, and demonstrations that measure accuracy, robustness, latency, and compute cost. Work with DSP and software engineers to integrate models into proof-of-concept systems and product platforms; communicate results and contribute to patents or conference papers. Education Graduate degree (MS or PhD) in machine learning, computer science, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent research experience. Skills Strong hands-on experience with modern audio understanding models, including sound event detection, SELD, acoustic scene analysis, or anomaly detection. Comfortable tackling complex, open-ended problems where you have to experiment with and discard many ideas before finding the right solution. Experience developing and evaluating deep learning models in PyTorch; strong Python skills. Understanding of audio representations, DSP, and evaluation metrics for detection, localization, and generalization. Experience with multimodal fusion (video, IMU, or other sensors) for context understanding is a plus. Experience with efficient inference, causal ML, ONNX/TFLite, embedded ML, or C/C++ is a plus. Strong communication skills; publications at conferences such as ICASSP, Interspeech, NeurIPS, or similar are welcome but not required. At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! items.desc: At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound. Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation. Description Job Description The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices for applications such as context understanding, dynamic awareness, augmented hearing and ones we haven’t yet imagined. You will work with experts in ML, DSP, software engineering, and psychoacoustics to prototype and implement new algorithms. You will develop audio understanding algorithms that enable devices to recognize what is happening in the world around them. Areas of interest include sound event detection and localization (SELD), acoustic scene understanding, unusual or anomalous sound detection, and multimodal context understanding from audio, video, and motion sensors. Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next. Responsibilities Research, prototype, train, and evaluate novel audio understanding models, from early experiments through real-time deployment on devices. Develop robust methods for sound event detection/localization, acoustic anomaly detection, and context-aware audio interpretation. Explore multimodal approaches that combine microphone signals with video, IMU, or other sensor data when useful. Build and curate datasets and data piplines, evaluation protocols, and demonstrations that measure accuracy, robustness, latency, and compute cost. Work with DSP and software engineers to integrate models into proof-of-concept systems and product platforms; communicate results and contribute to patents or conference papers. Education Graduate degree (MS or PhD) in machine learning, computer science, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent research experience. Skills Strong hands-on experience with modern audio understanding models, including sound event detection, SELD, acoustic scene analysis, or anomaly detection. Comfortable tackling complex, open-ended problems where you have to experiment with and discard many ideas before finding the right solution. Experience developing and evaluating deep learning models in PyTorch; strong Python skills. Understanding of audio representations, DSP, and evaluation metrics for detection, localization, and generalization. Experience with multimodal fusion (video, IMU, or other sensors) for context understanding is a plus. Experience with efficient inference, causal ML, ONNX/TFLite, embedded ML, or C/C++ is a plus. Strong communication skills; publications at conferences such as ICASSP, Interspeech, NeurIPS, or similar are welcome but not required. items.desc: Remote/Hybrid | Full-time About Fluid Concepts Fluid Concepts is a data research lab building the data and methods needed for frontier multimodal, human-centric, and interactive AI. We design and produce research-grade datasets for capabilities that are difficult to capture synthetically: natural conversation, social interaction, multimodal behavior, tool use, embodied interaction, and other forms of complex human behavior. We’re looking for a Founding Research Scientist / Engineer to help turn those datasets into research infrastructure, evaluations, models, and scientific results. The Role This is a hands-on research and engineering role spanning the full lifecycle of our work: building tools for data collection, developing novel evaluations, post-training models on proprietary data, and publishing the resulting research. You’ll work closely with our research, engineering, and collection teams, moving between experimental ideas and working systems. We’re especially interested in people who enjoy building things in order to answer research questions — and doing research in order to decide what should be built next. What You’ll Do Build tooling for novel data collections Support the software and experimental environments used to collect complex human interaction data. You Might: Build applications, interfaces, and experimental tools used by participants during collections Instrument collection environments to capture synchronized behavioral, interaction, and system data Develop internal tools for monitoring, inspecting, and validating data during collection Prototype new collection workflows quickly and support them during pilots and production Work with research, design, and operations to turn experimental protocols into robust systems The goal is not general-purpose infrastructure for its own sake: it is building the tools required to collect data that otherwise would not exist. Develop evaluations for interactive intelligence Turn our datasets — and relevant external datasets — into rigorous evaluations of emerging model capabilities. This Could Include: Designing benchmark tasks around conversation, speech, social behavior, multimodal interaction, and tool use Defining evaluation protocols, metrics, baselines, and model interfaces Building reusable evaluation harnesses across APIs and open-weight models Developing causal or controlled evaluation methods that isolate specific interactional capabilities Analyzing model behavior and identifying where current systems fail Connecting dataset properties to measurable differences in model performance We care particularly about evaluations that move beyond static question answering and measure how models perceive, reason about, and participate in interaction over time. Post-train models on proprietary data Use Fluid datasets to investigate whether targeted data can unlock new model capabilities. You Might: Fine-tune or otherwise post-train speech, language, or multimodal models Design experiments comparing data mixtures, supervision strategies, and training objectives Develop models for capabilities such as social inference, conversational coordination, or multimodal understanding Build training and evaluation pipelines for rapid experimentation Study how model behavior changes as a function of data composition and scale Produce compelling demonstrations of capabilities enabled by our data An example might be post-training a multimodal model on proprietary social-interaction data and testing whether it becomes better at inferring relationships, rapport, intent, or other latent social properties. Publish scientific research Turn our datasets, methods, evaluations, and model experiments into work that advances the scientific community. You Will: Formulate research questions around our datasets and methods Design and execute experiments Analyze and communicate results clearly Contribute to papers, benchmarks, and dataset releases Publish at leading ML, speech, multimodal, and HCI venues Help establish Fluid as a scientific contributor to the fields in which we operate Publishing is not separate from the product work: strong scientific results help us understand whether the datasets and methods we build actually matter. What This Might Look Like Day To Day One week, you might be building a web application that captures synchronized participant actions and tool calls during a new conversational dataset pilot. The next, you might turn that dataset into an evaluation harness, run several frontier and open-weight models against it, and identify a specific interactional behavior where existing systems fail. You might then post-train a model on a subset of Fluid’s proprietary data, measure whether that capability improves, and work with the team to turn the result into a benchmark, demonstration, or paper. The work moves continuously between tooling, experimentation, modeling, evaluation, and scientific communication. Who We’re Looking For We’re looking for someone who …

items.desc: Position description Category Electronics components and equipments Contract Fixed-term contract Job title Research Engineer in Design Space Exploration Optimization OR/AI H/F Socio-professional category Executive Contract duration (months) 24 Job description Exploring and Optimizing Next-Generation Computing Architectures Designing modern computing systems involves navigating increasingly complex design spaces, with numerous architectural, hardware and software parameters to consider. The emergence of heterogeneous Systems-on-Chip (SoCs) and chiplet-based architectures brings new opportunities, but also additional challenges in selecting processing elements, accelerators, memory hierarchies, interconnects and hardware-software mappings. At CEA-List, our research team is developing A-DECA (Automated Design Space Exploration for Computing Architectures), a framework dedicated to the automated exploration and optimization of complex computing architectures. By combining architectural models, simulation tools and optimization algorithms, A-DECA aims to efficiently explore design alternatives and identify promising configurations and Pareto-optimal trade-offs. The position offers the opportunity to contribute to this research by developing innovative methodologies for scalable, multi-objective design-space exploration. The work will draw on techniques from combinatorial optimization, operations research, machine learning and artificial intelligence to address the challenges of exploring increasingly large and complex architectural design spaces. Your Role and Research Activities As part of the research team at CEA-List, you will contribute to the development of new optimization methodologies and the continued evolution of A-DECA. Your work will combine algorithmic research, software development and practical applications to complex computing systems. Depending on your expertise, you will have the opportunity to explore different optimization strategies and contribute to their integration and evaluation within A-DECA. Your activities will include: Modeling architecture exploration problems: Identify design variables, constraints, objective functions and relevant system-level performance indicators. Developing scalable exploration methodologies: Address large and heterogeneous design spaces involving discrete, continuous and mixed-variable optimization problems. Investigating optimization algorithms: Study and implement multi-objective and combinatorial optimization techniques to identify promising architectural configurations and trade-offs. Exploring hybrid optimization strategies: Combine approaches from operations research, metaheuristics and machine learning/AI to improve design-space exploration. Extending the A-DECA framework: Develop reusable APIs and orchestration mechanisms to facilitate the integration of simulation tools, evaluation metrics and optimization algorithms. Evaluating and comparing methodologies: Design benchmarks and experimental protocols to assess solution quality, convergence speed, robustness and computational cost. Applying research to computing architectures Contributing to research outcomes Applicant Profile We are looking for a candidate with a strong interest in optimization algorithms, complex systems and research-oriented software development, who is motivated to explore new approaches and apply them to challenging engineering problems. items.desc: Context and motivation Diffusion-based models can generate diverse 3D human motions [1], but inferring and generating the camera wearer’s full-body movement from first-person observations remains difficult because the body is largely out of view and camera motion is ambiguous. Recent egocentric methods, including UniEgoMotion [2], and datasets such as Ego-Exo4D [3] provide promising foundations. External motion corpora such as AMASS [4] and Motion-X [5] contain complementary movement variations. The proposed internship investigates whether generating additional 3D motion samples from external motion priors, then assessing their physical plausibility, can improve downstream egocentric motion generation. Merely increasing synthetic sample count may not help: quality, diversity, and alignment with first-person conditioning must be evaluated. Research objectives Generate diverse synthetic 3D human motion samples using an existing motion generator trained or adapted on AMASS and/or Motion-X. Assess anatomical plausibility, foot contact/sliding, ground penetration, temporal continuity, and redundancy; construct quality-controlled synthetic data. Transfer augmented motion knowledge to egocentric generation via motion-prior pretraining/fine-tuning and, if feasible, synthetic head-motion/body-motion conditioning. Demonstrate whether augmentation improves realism, diversity, physical quality, and generalization relative to strong baselines. Proposed methodology Dataset harmonization Inspect access and annotation coverage; convert selected motion sequences into a common skeleton, coordinate convention, root trajectory, joint rotation representation, and frame rate. Use only validated Ego-Exo4D observation–motion pairs for supervised egocentric training and testing [3]. Generative augmentation Reuse or adapt a pretrained diffusion-based motion generator such as MDM [1] on external motion datasets [4,5]. Sample novel motion sequences with controlled actions or text conditions where supported; assess novelty and dataset coverage rather than assuming generated motions are genuinely new. Physical quality control Implement measurable anatomical, contact, ground, and temporal quality indicators. Compare unfiltered and filtered synthetic samples with matched sample counts, and monitor whether filtering removes rare but valid motions. Egocentric transfer and evaluation First establish an ego-only baseline inspired by methods such as UniEgoMotion [2]. Compare real external motion-prior pretraining, additional synthetic motion pretraining, and physically filtered augmentation. As an extension, derive head trajectories from generated full-body motions to construct synthetic head-motion/body-motion pairs. These are not equivalent to realistic egocentric RGB video; the downstream conditioning modality must be specified.Evaluate head trajectory consistency, physical violation rates, motion diversity, held-out actions, and paired 3D pose errors where ground truth is available. Include controlled ablations and computational cost. First-person personalized demonstrator Build an independent first-person (egocentric) demonstrator focused on the camera wearer’s own motion. Users may upload supported first-person observations or select validated examples, run the egocentric pipeline, inspect a generated full-body 3D avatar animation, compare candidate motions, and export motion in a documented format.The demonstrator may optionally accept a compatible user-provided movement reference if the selected model supports that conditioning. Arbitrary first-person RGB input and personalized generation are stretch capabilities contingent on pretrained model support. Expected outcomes Reproducible motion harmonization and synthetic generation pipeline. Physical quality scoring and filtered/unfiltered augmented datasets. Downstream egocentric baseline and augmentation comparisons with ablations. Standalone first-person motion demonstrator, source code, and documentation. Internship report and, subject to results, a research paper draft. Timeline and Research Lab The research is expected to be conducted for six months with the results to be communicated in the Master Thesis and possibly a publication (an international conference or journal, depending on the results achieved). The research will be carried out within the ARTEMIS department of Télécom SudParis, ARMEDIA team and SAMOVAR laboratory, in conjunction with MocapLab company for study cases. ---------- Applications Requirements ---------- Candidate profile The internship is intended for Master's (M2) or final-year engineering students specializing in Artificial Intelligence, Computer Vision, Computer Graphics, or related fields. items.card: What you'll do Help improve and test the arrhythmia-classification algorithms, especially on noisy, real-world recordings. Implement and compare methods for ECG interval detection (PR, QRS, QT/QTc, RR) under the guidance of senior team members. Work on signal-quality steps such as filtering, baseline-wander removal, and artifact detection. Help build and evaluate the ECG digitisation pipeline. This turns scanned or
items.desc: We're looking for a Research Intern or Junior Data Scientist to help improve the algorithms behind our ECG analysis platform. You'll work alongside experienced data scientists, ECG technicians, and engineers on arrhythmia classification, ECG interval detection (PR, QRS, QT), signal quality, and ECG digitisation (turning paper or image ECGs into digital signals). If you're curious about biosignals, enjoy hands-on experiments, and want to learn how algorithms get to clinical grade, we'd love to hear from you. What you'll do Help improve and test the arrhythmia-classification algorithms, especially on noisy, real-world recordings. Implement and compare methods for ECG interval detection (PR, QRS, QT/QTc, RR) under the guidance of senior team members. Work on signal-quality steps such as filtering, baseline-wander removal, and artifact detection. Help build and evaluate the ECG digitisation pipeline. This turns scanned or photographed paper ECGs into usable digital signals. It involves grid detection and removal, finding the boundaries of each lead, extracting the signal trace, and calibrating amplitude and time (mm/mV, 25 mm/s). Run experiments and evaluations against reference annotations, and report results clearly: classification metrics, interval errors, and digitisation accuracy. Support the annotation team by preparing data, checking label quality and summarising disagreements. Document code, datasets and experiments so the work can be reproduced and supports quality and regulatory requirements. Required skills (must-have) Good Python skills and familiarity with NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Matplotlib and scikit-learn. Basic signal-processing knowledge: sampling, frequency content, filters (low-pass, high-pass, band-pass) and the Fourier transform. Basic image-processing knowledge (e.g., OpenCV or scikit-image): thresholding, morphology, edge or line detection and contours. This is used for ECG digitisation. Understanding of core machine-learning concepts: train/validation/test splits, overfitting, cross-validation and common classifiers. Familiarity with evaluation metrics such as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision/PPV, F1 and AUC, and an understanding of why accuracy alone is misleading on imbalanced data. Working knowledge of Git and of writing clean, commented code or notebooks. Eagerness to learn, attention to detail, and comfort asking questions and taking feedback. Comfort using AI assistants such as Claude to speed up coding, prototyping, and learning, while checking and understanding what they produce. Preferred / nice-to-have A degree in progress or recently completed in biomedical engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, physics, data science, or a related field. Coursework, a thesis, or personal projects involving ECG, EEG, PPG, or other biosignal or time-series data. Some exposure to ECG basics: P wave, QRS complex, T wave, and common rhythms such as sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation. Awareness of classical ECG methods such as Pan-Tompkins QRS detection or wavelet-based delineation, or of open-source tools like NeuroKit2, WFDB, or BioSPPy. Experience with public ECG datasets such as the PhysioNet databases (MIT-BIH, QT Database), LUDB, or PTB-XL. Interest in ECG-image work, for example the PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2024 on ECG image digitisation, or synthetic ECG image generators such as ECG-Image-Kit. Basic deep learning with PyTorch or TensorFlow/Keras, e.g., a simple 1-D CNN for signals or a CNN or U-Net for images. Interest in medical devices and healthcare regulation (ISO 13485, IEC 62304, CE/MDR). No prior experience needed. What you'll gain Mentorship from experienced data scientists and clinical ECG experts. Hands-on work with real-world ECG data in a regulated medical-device product. Experience across the whole algorithm workflow: data preparation, method development, validation, and documentation.

items.desc: THE OPPORTUNITY IN A NUTSHELL You? A curious, hands-on Data Scientist with around 3+ years of experience, who loves training models, getting them into production, and proving with data that they make things better. Role? Data Scientist in Discovery, the team behind search and recommendations for all of Vend's marketplaces, building the models that help millions of people find what they're looking for. Tech stack? Python, PyTorch and SQL. Multimodal embedding models, two-tower and collaborative filtering recommenders, and semantic and hybrid search, trained on our own GPU platform on GCP. Company? Vend, home of FINN, Blocket, Tori, Oikotie, DBA & Bilbasen, where millions of people across the Nordics connect to find what they need, whether it's a job, a home, a way to move, or a fresh start. Location? Join us in our Oslo office, with the flexibility to work 3 days per week remotely! WHY US? Curious how search can understand what people mean, not just what they type? Your models reach everyone using our marketplaces, with a direct line to the business: our latest multimodal recommender lifted clicks, favourites, messages and purchases by 8 to 11%. And you'll learn from an experienced Lead Data Scientist. Real scale. Millions of searches a day across our verticals and the Nordics. Today we have over 300 million total visits every month! A shared platform that handles serving and rollout, so you can focus on the models. Open modelling problems: multimodal embeddings, hybrid search, and relevance that is never really "done". A company where search is the product, not just a feature. Data scientists and engineers in the same team, so your models reach production. One of the largest user datasets in the Nordics, and plenty of opportunities we haven’t had time to explore yet. Sounds like your cup of tea? Check out the details below! WHO ARE YOU? You have around 3+ years of hands-on experience training and deploying ML models. You're strong in Python and PyTorch and have worked with embedding or retrieval models such as two-tower models, sentence transformers or contrastive learning. You take models all the way to production and own them afterwards: retraining, monitoring, debugging and improving. We care most about models that make it out of the notebook. You're rigorous about evaluation. You know offline metrics like NDCG and recall@k, design A/B tests that hold up, and understand why click data can lie to you, from position bias to feedback loops. You're comfortable with data at scale. You write solid SQL, build training datasets from raw event data, and don't mind digging into why a field suddenly went missing. You're curious about the product and use AI tools with intent. You ask what we're really trying to improve before choosing the metric, and use tools like Claude Code to move faster without losing rigour. You communicate well in English, as it's our working language. Join a team of passionate thinkers, innovators, and dreamers — and help us connect people and build communities to create economic opportunity for all. Who Are We? The Product Knowledge team is at the epicenter of eBay’s Tech-driven, Customer-centric overhaul. Our team is entrusted with creating and using eBay’s Product Knowledge - a vast Big Data system which is built up of listings, transactions, products, knowledge graphs, and more. Our team has a mix of highly proficient people from multiple fields such as Machine Learning, Data Science, Software Engineering, Operations, and Big Data Analytics. We have a strong culture of collaboration, and plenty of opportunity to learn, make an impact, and grow! What Will You Do We are looking for Applied Researchers to join our Annotation Science team and advance how eBay understands and connects millions of marketplace listings to products. Our researchers tackle challenging problems in Product Matching, Multimodal AI, Entity Resolution, and Agentic AI , developing accurate, scalable solutions using text, images, and structured data. From building cutting-edge ML models to leveraging LLMs and agentic workflows, our work powers better search, discovery, and selling experiences. If you're passionate about solving complex AI challenges and bringing innovative research into production at scale, we'd love to hear from you! What you will accomplish: Drive applied research in Product Matching, Entity Resolution, and Multimodal AI to connect millions of eBay listings to structured product knowledge at scale. Design and build ML models and LLM-powered pipelines that improve search relevance, product discovery, and selling experiences for buyers and sellers across multilingual markets. Develop and deploy AI workflows that bring innovative research solutions into production systems handling real-world marketplace data. Advance eBay's science by creating accurate, scalable approaches that leverage text, images, and structured data to understand marketplace listings. Collaborate across Machine Learning, Data Science, Software Engineering, and Data Analytics to translate research breakthroughs into measurable business impact. What you will bring: Education: Ph.D. or M.S. in Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related field with a focus on machine learning or data science. Experience: 2-4 years (with PhD) or 4-6 years (with MS) Experience: Experience in applied research or development of machine learning models, data analysis, preferably with the advertising industry or a closely related field, i.e. search, recommender system and NLP. Technical Proficiency: Strong programming skills in Python, Scala, or similar languages. Expertise in machine learning frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) and experience with big data technologies (e.g., Hadoop, Spark). Analytical Skills: Outstanding ability to analyze large datasets, and derive actionable insights. Expertise in data mining and segmentation. Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to convey sophisticated technical concepts to non-technical partners. Additional Details eBay is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, and disability, or other legally protected status.  Research Intern – Machine Learning for Power Systems 
 Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. Improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?
 Transform the everyday with us! 
 You will join the Physics-Informed AI research group within Siemens’ Data and Artificial Intelligence organization — our central research hub for artificial intelligence — for a Spring 2027 internship. 
 We are looking for a Research Intern in Machine Learning for Power Systems. This position will be remote. 
 You’ll make an impact by: 
 Developing machine learning algorithms for power systems.
 Using artificial intelligence to speed up simulations, improve forecasting, and strengthen the cybersecurity posture of the power grid.
 Exploring foundation models for engineering data modalities such as tabular and time-series data.
 Embedding physics into generative artificial intelligence models for power system applications.
 Working on fast-paced co-creation projects with quickly changing requirements at the intersection of machine learning and power systems.
 Building demonstrators, supporting technology transition to Siemens businesses, and documenting your work through technical reports and academic publications.
 You’ll win us over by having the following qualifications: 
 Basic Qualifications: 
 • Currently enrolled as a PhD student in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
 • Research experience applying artificial intelligence and machine learning to power systems.
 • Experience designing and applying graph neural networks for power system applications.
 • Proficiency in Python, PyTorch, and PyTorch Geometric (PyG), and in the effective use of agentic coding tools.
 • Minimal travel required (less than 10%).
 • Legally authorized to work in the United States on a continual and permanent basis without company sponsorship.
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Research experience with foundation models for engineering data modalities beyond language and image, such as tabular or time-series data.
 Experience embedding physics into generative artificial intelligence models.
 Publications at leading artificial intelligence venues (for example, NeurIPS, ICML, or ICLR) or power systems venues (for example, IEEE PES).

They are an integral part of our Business Conduct Guidelines and our corporate strategy.

items.desc: Turba Labs · Heidelberg (Germany) or San Francisco Bay Area (USA) · On-site, hybrid or remote · Full-time · Candidates must live in Germany or the USA A scheduling idea that works in a notebook is a rumor until it survives a client's cluster. Data centers now run mixed clusters of GPU generations, vendors and accelerators, and the software that schedules work on them was mostly built for uniform hardware. Turba Labs is building what replaces it, and it has to work on infrastructure we do not control. Two products. The Scheduler runs live on our clients' infrastructure and decides which workload runs on which GPU, and when. The Simulator answers a related question before a data center spends a cent: given a planned build-out, what is the best way to use it? You make what we build reliable enough for a data center to depend on. What you will own From idea to production. Take a validated idea into the Scheduler: design it, build it, test it, roll it out, monitor it, and own what happens after. The ML platform's architecture. The decisions others build on, including when a learned approach earns its operational cost over a simple heuristic. Training, evaluation and benchmarking pipelines. Every scheduling policy and performance model reproducible and comparable, so progress is measured, not argued. GPU-level reality. Profile and optimize workloads and models on heterogeneous hardware, and feed what you measure back into the Simulator. Safe failure. Guardrails, fallbacks and observability, so the system running on infrastructure we do not control degrades gracefully, never dramatically. The interfaces. Clear contracts and release plans with the infrastructure and product engineers around you. Who you are You have shipped ML into production and carry the operational weight, not just the model. You are strong in Python and PyTorch and practice real software engineering: tests, review, CI, and design that survives the next person. You think in trade-offs between accuracy, latency, cost and risk, and you can say why you chose what you chose. You are comfortable close to the hardware, or hungry to be. You write designs and tickets that others can execute without a follow-up call. We do not screen on years or titles. We screen on the hardest system you have shipped and how deeply you understood it. A plus GPU performance work: profiling, CUDA, inference engines such as vLLM or TensorRT, distributed training. Experience with cluster or workload schedulers, Linux systems work and Docker. Reinforcement learning, optimization or simulation in a production setting. Deploying software into customer-managed or on-premises environments. Why this This is infrastructure software that changes how AI compute gets used. What you ship here runs on real hardware in real data centers, with real money on the line, alongside the data scientists who design the methods. About us Turba Labs is an innovative, emerging startup that transforms AI laws. We are a team of passionate problem-solvers who believe in what we’re building. We constantly push boundaries and embrace our inner nerds as we find new ways to tackle complex challenges. You will find a dynamic work environment here, with flat or even non-existent hierarchies and the chance to take on responsibility from day one. Turba Labs is committed to providing a respectful, safe, and inclusive workplace. Diversity means fostering an environment where individual differences are recognized, valued, and respected, enabling everyone to fully contribute their talents and strengths. This commitment begins with our recruitment process. If you require any accommodations to support your application or interview, please let us know as we are happy to assist.

items.desc: Arbetsuppgifter Institutionen för robotik, perception och lärande söker en forskningsingenjör för SPRINT, ett agilt projekt inom TECoSA (Center for Trustworthy Edge Computing Systems and Applications). Du kommer att ingå i ett tvärvetenskapligt team av forskare från institutionerna för robotik, perception och lärande, nätverks- och systemteknik samt datavetenskap och lärande. Projektet kommer att utveckla ett återanvändbart och modulärt ramverk för implementering och utvärdering av accelererad inferens på edge-enheter i uppgiftsorienterade konversationssystem. Arbetsuppgifterna omfattar implementering av komponenter för inferens och prestandaövervakning, integration av ramverket med en konversationsrobot samt stöd vid pilotinteraktioner, användarstudier, mjukvarulansering och den avslutande demonstrationen. Kvalifikationer Krav Avlagd examen på grundnivå eller avancerad nivå (högskoleutbildning) inom ämnet för anställningen eller motsvarande kompetens. Mycket goda kunskaper i Python-programmering samt erfarenhet av maskininlärningsramverk och verktyg såsom PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers eller motsvarande. Förmåga att arbeta både självständigt och i samarbete med andra i en tvärvetenskaplig forskningsmiljö. God förmåga att uttrycka sig i tal och skrift på engelska då det krävs i det dagliga arbetet. Meriterande Erfarenhet av Linux, Git, dataanalys och reproducerbara experimentella arbetssätt. Erfarenhet av utveckling och utvärdering av maskininlärningssystem eller annan jämförbar dataintensiv programvara. Erfarenhet av experimentella testmiljöer, nätverkskonfiguration eller mätning av system- och nätverksprestanda. Erfarenhet av driftsättning på edge-enheter eller GPU:er samt prestandaprofilering. Erfarenhet av arbete med stora språkmodeller (LLM). Erfarenhet av arbete med Furhat eller liknande plattformar för konversationsrobotar. Erfarenhet av reproducerbara experiment, dataanalys och forskningsprogramvara. Medvetenhet om mångfalds- och likabehandlingsfrågor med särskild fokus på jämställdhet. Vi kommer lägga stor vikt vid personliga egenskaper. Bli en del av KTH KTH formar framtiden genom utbildning, forskning och innovation. Som ett ledande internationellt tekniskt universitet spelar vi en aktiv roll i att driva och medverka i omställningen till ett hållbart samhälle. Här erbjuds du möjligheten att växa och utvecklas på en kreativ och dynamisk arbetsplats med goda arbetsvillkor och förmåner. Jämställdhet, mångfald och lika villkor är en kvalitetsfråga och en självklar del av KTH:s värdegrund som universitet och statlig myndighet. Läs mer om våra förmåner och hur det är att arbeta och utvecklas på KTH. Fackliga representanter Kontaktuppgiftertill fackliga representanter. Ansökan Du ansöker via KTH:s rekryteringssystem. Du som sökande har huvudansvaret för att din ansökan är komplett när den skickas in. Ansökan ska innehålla: CV inklusive relevant yrkeserfarenhet och kunskap. Kopia av examensbevis och betyg från dina tidigare universitetsstudier. Översättningar till engelska eller svenska om de ursprungliga dokumenten inte utfärdas på något av dessa språk. Ansökan ska vara KTH tillhanda senast sista ansökningsdagen vid midnatt, CET/CEST (CentralEuropean Time/Central European Summer Time). Om anställningen Anställningen gäller tidsbegränsat enligt avtal - i upp till 6 mån, med tillträde enligt överenskommelse. Övrigt För information om behandling av personuppgifter i samband med rekrytering. Det kan förekomma att en anställning hos KTH är placerad i säkerhetsklass. Om så är fallet för just denna anställning görs en säkerhetsprövning av sökande i enlighet med säkerhetsskyddslagen (2018:585) efter samtycke. I dessa fall är en förutsättning för anställning att sökande blir godkänd efter säkerhetsprövning. Vi undanber oss direktkontakt med bemannings- och rekryteringsföretag samt försäljare av platsannonser.

Our technology leadership makes us the partner of choice for hundreds of governments and thousands of enterprises in over 180 countries, including some of the biggest and most influential brands in the world. In applying our unique expertise in biometrics and cryptography , we enable our clients to unlock simpler and safer ways to pay, connect, access, identify, travel and protect public places – at scale and in total security. Our teams work from 5 continents and speak 100+ different languages. We strongly believe that our diversity is a key driver of innovation and performance. Purpose This internship focuses on studying and evaluating neural network compression techniques applied to biometric fraud detection. As deep learning models become increasingly complex, optimizing their architecture and computational requirements is essential to improving their efficiency and enabling their deployment in real-world applications. The objective of this internship is to investigate different model compression techniques to address four key challenges: Optimizing inference time to improve model execution speed Reducing memory footprint to make models more lightweight Potentially accelerating training through more efficient architectures and techniques Enabling the use of larger and more powerful models while controlling computational costs The Project Will Focus On Three Main Research Areas Low-Rank Decomposition: Exploring and adapting low-rank decomposition techniques to convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and hybrid Vision Transformer-CNN architectures Quantization: Investigating model quantization, particularly INT8 formats, through Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) and Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) Pruning and Sparsity: Studying techniques to reduce model complexity by removing redundant parameters and introducing sparsity Key Missions Conduct a scientific literature review to identify and understand state-of-the-art neural network compression techniques Select relevant approaches and adapt, implement and experiment with the most promising methods Evaluate their performance, analyze the results, identify limitations and investigate potential improvements Profile & Other Information Education Final-year engineering student or Master's degree (M2) student specializing in Computer items.desc: About Pavo Pavo is building the Applied Science Factory: systems that develop an understanding of production ML, investigate performance, construct reliable evaluations, and help engineers make measurable improvements. We work with product behavior, code, data, models, and experiment history across real production systems. Our research covers training environments, scientific agent capabilities, and models for structured and behavioral data. We're a small team of researchers and engineers. Members of Technical Staff help define their research agenda and own the experiments, implementation, and evaluation end to end. The role Pavo's Applied Science Factory reconstructs production systems, investigates performance, formulates hypotheses, constructs evaluations, and guides improvements through human checkpoints. You'll research how to train models that perform the scientific work within this loop. Example capabilities include selecting appropriate offline estimators, checking counterfactual assumptions, explaining offline–online discrepancies, designing experiments, and working through multi-step investigations using code and data tools. You'll own the model-training research loop: task and trajectory data, supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, reward and verifier design, rollout analysis, ablations, and held-out evaluation. You'll study which improvements generalize across different production systems and collaborate with the Environments owner on training tasks and verifiers. What you'll build Construct training tasks and expert/agent trajectories covering scientific investigation, cohort analysis, evaluation design, and causal reasoning. Develop SFT and RL post-training recipes, including data mixtures, curricula, reward signals, verifier design, and model selection. Run reproducible training and long-horizon agent rollouts with code execution, data queries, and retrieval; inspect trajectories, training stability, and failure modes. Build versioned held-out evaluations for estimator correctness, assumption checking, evidence quality, reward exploits, and cross-system regressions. Use ablations, failure analysis, and real applied-science workflows to establish measurable model capability improvements. What we look for Evidence that you personally improved a model through training or post-training, with concrete baselines, ablations, error analysis, and generalization results. Strong Python and PyTorch or JAX; hands-on SFT, reinforcement learning, preference or reward modeling, or policy optimization. Experience owning training runs end to end: dataset construction, rollout workers, checkpoints, experiment tracking, evaluation, and reproducibility. Ability to design verifiable rewards and robust held-out evaluations, detect reward hacking, and investigate training failures. Strong experimental judgment; experience in causal inference, offline policy evaluation, recommendation systems, or production experimentation is useful. What we offer Define and own a substantial research direction, with responsibility for the experiments, engineering, and deployment. Work with real production data, experiment histories, and feedback from systems across different businesses. Work directly with the founders and a small team with strong research and engineering backgrounds, including experience building ML systems serving 500M+ users. Publish papers, technical reports, talks, or open-source work where the results and customer confidentiality permit. Pavo is an equal opportunity employer.

items.desc: MACHINE LEARNING ENGINEER – HUMANOID ROBOTICS Schiedam (Rotterdam area) · On-site · Full-time Put humanoid robots to work in the real world, hands-on with the latest robotics and AI technology. About HAC At the Humanoid Application Center (HAC) we believe humanoid robotics will become a flexible, universal automation layer that fundamentally changes how physical work gets done. Together with partner companies, we work on real-world use cases in manufacturing, logistics, agriculture and facility services, and we’re building the team and the internal software stack to make this possible. All of this happens in our own humanoid robotics lab in Schiedam, where we train and test with robots such as the AgiBot G2, UBTech Cruzr Y and Unitree G1. Your role You’ll be the ML specialist on a small, cross-disciplinary engineering team. The core challenge in humanoids is closing the gap between impressive demos and reliable deployment in real work environments. You work on the learning side of that gap: imitation learning, reinforcement learning, VLAs and world models, trained and deployed on real hardware. We’re a small team of around 15 people, which means short lines, lots of ownership and a direct impact on what we build. What you’ll do - Train, fine-tune and deploy models across the range, from small embedded models to foundation models, VLMs and world models - Build and own our learning loops: teleop data collection, dataset curation, training pipelines, evaluation and redeployment - Develop imitation learning and reinforcement learning policies for manipulation and locomotion, in simulation and on hardware - Build out our simulation environments (Isaac Sim/Lab, MuJoCo or similar) for training, evaluation and sim-to-real transfer - Take partner use cases from “not yet possible” to demonstrated and deployed What you bring - Hands-on experience training deep learning models yourself, not only using them via APIs - Solid Python and PyTorch (or JAX) - Experience deploying models to embedded hardware (quantization, TensorRT, ONNX or similar) - An MSc or PhD in ML, AI, robotics or CS, or equivalent demonstrated experience - The right to work in the Netherlands (see below) Strong pluses: RL or IL on real robots, sim-to-real, ROS 2, VLAs, world models, diffusion policies and MLOps practice. We care more about what you’ve built than formal years of experience. We value complementary backgrounds and encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. What we offer - A lab full of state-of-the-art humanoid robots: train a model in the morning, run it on hardware in the afternoon - Real industrial use cases with committed partners - Founding-stage influence on our stack and the way we work - A hands-on, international team at MICS in Schiedam How to apply Apply via LinkedIn or send an email to sander@humanoidcenter.nl with your CV and a short description of the most interesting or challenging project you’ve worked on: what the problem was, what you built and what you learned. This part weighs heavily. GitHub, papers or project links are very welcome. Please note: we are unable to offer visa sponsorship or relocation support. To be considered, you must already have the right to work in the Netherlands, for example as an EU/EEA or Swiss citizen, or with a valid Dutch residence permit that allows you to work. Our process: after reviewing your application, we’ll invite you for a 30-minute online intro call. Next is an on-site assessment of about 1.5 hours at our lab, where you’ll get a tour, present some of your work and go through a few of our real cases with the team. Questions first? Reach us via sander@humanoidcenter.nl

items.desc: Job Title Internship: Synthetic Data Generation for Dental AI (Master) Job Description Start Date: January/February 2027 Duration: minimum 6 months Type: Internship Weekly Presence: 40h (minimum 32h) Location: Eindhoven Internship: Synthetic Data Generation for Dental AI (Master) Philips has a long history of successfully introducing innovative products to the market (lamps, CD players, medical imaging equipment, patient monitors, etc). Today, Philips is 100% health technology company with Data and AI being an integral part of Philips strategy. This internship develops a scalable pipeline for generating photorealistic synthetic intraoral images and automatic ground-truth labels from 3D jaws. Tooth detection and instance segmentation are the primary validation case. The same approach should also support other intraoral AI algorithms, such as gumline localization and detection of cavities or other oral conditions. Building on previous work in 3D jaw reconstruction and SAM mask generation/distillation, the project will quantify how synthetic data affects accuracy, robustness and the synthetic-to-real domain gap. Your challenge: We are looking for an enthusiastic candidate who is passionate about computer vision, 3D graphics and deep learning. Your team: You will be working in the R&D department of Philips Oral Healthcare in Eindhoven. The department works on cross-domain competences required to develop cutting-edge oral healthcare innovations, like machine learning, microbiology, sensors, optical imaging. Your Role Review 3D/synthetic dental data, rendering and domain-randomization methods. Build a data-generation pipeline from reconstructed or parametric 3D jaws. Vary anatomy, camera pose, lighting, materials and oral conditions. Export images with masks, depth, normals and tooth labels. Train/evaluate tooth detection and identification models; report conclusions. Draft a technical note or paper; present results at a Philips R&D forum. You're The Right Fit If MSc. in Data Science, CS, AI, Mathematics, Physics or Biomedical Engineering. Experience with Python programming is essential. Good knowledge of deep learning and computer vision in PyTorch. Passion for 3D modelling, rendering and synthetic data generation. Experience with Blender, 3D reconstruction or generative AI. Language: good written and spoken English. Previous internship experience is not necessary but is a plus. Scientific publications are a big plus. Good communication skills and enthusiasm to work in an international team. How We Work Together We believe that we are better together than apart. For our office-based teams, this means working in-person at least 3 days per week. Onsite roles require full-time presence in the company’s facilities. Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations. Monthly full-time allowance between €500 - €700 gross, depending on your education level. If you need to relocate to The Netherlands specifically for the internship there will be a different allowance. Part-time internships receive the allowance pro-rata. Housing compensation, in case of relocating to the vicinity of the office, €300,- net if location is in the vicinity of Amsterdam, €255,- net for all other Philips locations. To be eligible, your usual home-work travel distance needs to be more than 50 km or 1.5 hours of travel time (one way). Afterwards, you need to provide the rental contract from your (new) landlord. Travel compensation, if you are not eligible for a free public transport (OV chipkaart - student travel product); you can receive max. €192,- net depending on your location. Paid holidays per internship term. About Philips We are a health technology company. We built our entire company around the belief that every human matters, and we won't stop until everybody everywhere has access to the quality healthcare that we all deserve. Do the work of your life to help the lives of others. Learn more about our business. Discover our rich and exciting history. Learn more about our purpose. If you’re interested in this role and have many, but not all, of the experiences needed, we encourage you to apply. You may still be the right candidate for this or other opportunities at Philips. Learn more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion here.

items.desc:
The Amazon Web Services (AWS) Center for Quantum Computing in Pasadena, CA, is looking to hire a Quantum Research Scientist in the Fabrication group. You will join a multi-disciplinary team of theoretical and experimental physicists, materials scientists, and hardware and software engineers working at the forefront of quantum computing. You should have a deep and broad knowledge of device fabrication techniques. 
Candidates with a track record of original scientific contributions will be preferred. We are looking for candidates with strong engineering principles, resourcefulness and a bias for action, superior problem solving, and excellent communication skills. Working effectively within a team environment is essential. As a research scientist you will be expected to work on new ideas and stay abreast of the field of experimental quantum computation. 
Key job responsibilities
In this role, you will drive improvements in quantum device performance. This will require designing experiments to assess the role of fabrication processes and artifacts on performance metrics, ensuring the collection of statistically significant data through automation, analyzing the results, and preparing clear summaries for the team. Finally, you will work with hardware engineers, material scientists, circuit designers, and measurement scientists to implement changes, collect measurement data, and assess the impact.
About the team
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
AWS Utility Computing (UC) provides product innovations — from foundational services such as Amazon’s Simple Storage Service (S3) and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), to consistently released new product innovations that continue to set AWS’s services and features apart in the industry. As a member of the UC organization, you’ll support the development and management of Compute, Database, Storage, Internet of Things (Iot), Platform, and Productivity Apps services in AWS. Within AWS UC, Amazon Dedicated Cloud (ADC) roles engage with AWS customers who require specialized security solutions for their cloud services.
Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
