items.desc: The GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences is one of the world's leading institutions in the field of geosciences. As part of the Helmholtz Association, Germany's largest research organisation, we address global challenges such as natural hazards, climate change and the sustainable use of resources. In doing so, we combine cutting-edge research with social relevance. Our international staff - around 1,200 employees and approx. 500 guests - work in a multidisciplinary way and with a unique infrastructure to research the dynamic processes of the Earth system. Our vision: "Taking the pulse of our Earth to safeguard a habitable planet." For section 2.1 "Physics of Earthquakes and Volcanoes" (department “Geophysics”), we are looking for a: Research scientist (f_m_x) - Seismology Reference Number 11691 Earthquakes induced by human activities, such as deep geothermal energy production, can cause ground shaking that raises concerns among local communities. Understanding earthquake source processes and predicting the resulting ground motions, including their uncertainties, are important for assessing seismic impacts and supporting transparent communication with stakeholders. Within the BMWE-funded collaborative project "Seismological Analysis and Societal Relevance of Deep Energy Projects (SAURIER)", GFZ is responsible for the subproject "TRansparent Interpretation and Characterisation of Earthquake RAdiation Patterns through probabilistic moment TensOr inversion and PGV Simulations (TRICERATOPS)". We are looking for a motivated researcher with a strong background in seismology and experience in earthquake source analysis and seismic waveform processing. The successful candidate will contribute to developing and applying probabilistic methods for earthquake source characterisation and physics-based ground motion modelling. The research will focus on quantifying the influence of earthquake source parameters and subsurface structure on predicted ground motions and their uncertainties, with the aim of estimating seismic impact zones. Fraunhofer IEG coordinates SAURIER and brings together seismological and social science research to improve the assessment and communication of induced seismicity. items.desc: Job description Do you want to develop new algorithms for large GPU systems inside established scientific codes, together with the people who build them? We are seeking a research engineer to join a project team of HPC software scientists at KTH Center for Scientific Computing (KCSC). The position is funded by SSF within the SEESSI project, which aims to ready Sweden's flagship codes for next-generation hardware: GROMACS (one of the most widely used molecular dynamics codes), Neko (a CFD framework nominated for the ACM Gordon Bell prize in 2023) and VeloxChem (a versatile open-source quantum chemistry software). At KCSC, code development, algorithm research and domain science sit side by side. You will work closely with the core developers and domain experts behind these codes: a team with a strong research track record in parallel algorithms and GPU acceleration, and vendor collaboration. Domain science experience is welcome but not required. Our aim goes beyond performance tuning: we redesign core algorithms for modern hardware, with energy efficiency as a design goal. Key research objectives: Mixed and reduced precision algorithms: using low-precision hardware in central kernels while keeping results accurate. Communication and data movement: communication schemes and data access strategies, e.g. GPU-initiated communication. Energy to solution: tracked alongside time to solution to guide algorithmic choices. You will have the opportunity to publish and present your work internationally and to contribute directly to the upstream codes. Qualifications Requirements A graduate degree or an advanced level (higher education) in the research subject or equivalent competence. Strong practical skills in modern C++ and/or Fortran. Hands-on experience with parallel programming for GPUs and distributed systems, e.g. CUDA, HIP, SYCL and MPI. Practical experience developing and optimizing an established scientific code on HPC systems at scale, including in-depth profiling, and a good grasp of how HPC codes are structured. Excellent English communication skills, as English is the working language of the team and its international collaborations. The ability to work independently and together with others. Preferred qualifications Doctoral studies in HPC or computational science. A background in numerical methods, e.g. error analysis for reduced precision. Experience with GPU communication, e.g. NVSHMEM, NCCL or GPU-aware MPI. Experience contributing to a large scientific code (e.g. MD, CFD or quantum chemistry). Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality. Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills. items.desc: På institutionen för filosofi, lingvistik och vetenskapsteori (FLoV) vid Humanistiska fakulteten har vi omkring 120 anställda och en undervisningsvolym som omfattar cirka 350 helårsstudenter. Hos oss pågår en mängd stora internationella och tvärvetenskapliga forskningsprojekt inom områden som teoretisk och praktisk filosofi, logik, lingvistik, datalingvistik, språkteknologi och vetenskapsteori. Vår forskning har många tillämpningar och samarbeten med andra vetenskapsområden, bland annat biologi, datavetenskap, ekonomi, idéhistoria, juridik, medicin, psykologi, religion, statsvetenskap och teknikvetenskap. Vi utbildar filosofer, logiker, lingvister, språkteknologer, vetenskapsteoretiker, filosofihistoriker och lärare i filosofi. Institutionen bedriver även forskarutbildning och utvecklingsarbete inom sina områden. Om du är intresserad av att arbeta i en internationell, dynamisk och samarbetsinriktad miljö, erbjuder FLoV en inspirerande plats för forskning och utbildning. Läs mer om oss här. Projektbeskrivning Det sexåriga RJ-programmet “ Change is Key! ” (läs mer här) pågår mellan 2022–2028 och leds av professor Nina Tahmasebi. Programmet har som huvudsyfte att ta fram beräkningsverktyg för att identifiera hur ord förändras över tid, vilket möjliggör för forskare som arbetar med stora textkorpusar att snabbt och effektivt utföra komplexa analyser. Dessa analyser kommer sedan att öka vår förståelse för hur ett stort antal språkliga, kulturella och sociala faktorer har förändrats över tid. Forskargruppen består av språkteknologer, lingvister, lexikografer, sociologer, genusforskare och litteraturvetare. Tre av fem delprojekt fokuserar på språkteknologi och NLP, ett ägnas åt utvärdering av befintliga språkhistoriska förändringshypoteser, och det sista delprojektet berör fyra humanistiska och samhällsvetenskapliga studier inklusive lexikografi. Programmet ger dig möjlighet att samarbeta med världsledande forskare och bidra till forskning med stort genomslag samt samförfattade publikationer i topprankade konferenser som ACL, NAACL och EMNLP. Inom forskningsprogrammet Change is Key! vid FLoV söks nu en forskare med specialisering på identifiering och analys av lexikala semantiska förändringar (LSF) från diakroniska texter med hjälp av beräkningsmodeller. Arbetsuppgifter Anställningens forskning ska bedrivas i ett forskningsprogram där språkteknologi utvecklas för språkhistoriska frågeställningar. Mer information om programmet finns här. Programmet utgör en aktiv och levande forskningsmiljö för detta spännande och växande forskningsfält kring LSF. Arbetet kommer att bestå av forskning inom LSF men också inom samhällsvetenskap och humaniora genom vårt samarbete inom programmet med forskare inom historisk lingvistik, analytisk sociologi, genusvetenskap, idéhistoria, samt litteraturvetenskap. En mindre del av anställningen kan innefatta arbetsuppgifter andra än forskning, som är relevanta för programmet samt pedagogiskt utvecklingsarbete för tutorials och sommarkurser. Inom kontexten för programmet samarbetar vi genom regelbundna möten där det är viktigt att ta en aktiv del i diskussioner och presentera resultat. Forskaren skall bidra till vetenskapliga framsteg som presenteras i samförfattade tidskriftsartiklar, samt vid nationella och internationella konferenser. Nu när forskningsprojektet går in i sitt sista år söker vi en mångsidig forskare som kan bidra till flera pågående forskningsprojekt, med fokus på att stödja deras slutförande och säkerställa att projektens mål och förväntade resultat uppnås. Huvuddelen av arbetet ska utföras på plats vid Göteborgs universitet. Forskaren förväntas delta aktivt i forskningsgruppens arbete och i ämnets workshopar, seminarier och konferenser, där arbetsspråket är engelska. Kvalifikationer Behörig till anställningen som forskare är den som har avlagt masterexamen eller motsvarande utländsk examen som bedöms likvärdig. Doktorsexamen inom ett för anställningen relevant ämnesområde är särskilt meriterande och kommer att väga tungt vid bedömningen av de sökandes kvalifikationer. Masteruppsatsen/doktorsavhandlingen ska vara inom ett forskningsområde som är relevant för den ovan beskrivna ämnesinriktningen (t ex språkteknologi, datavetenskap med inriktning på språkteknologi, lingvistik med beräknings- eller modelleringserfarenhet, informationsvetenskaper, eller matematik med erfarenhet av språkliga data). Viktigast vid bedömningen av de sökande är deras vetenskapliga skicklighet, där särskild vikt kommer att läggas vid den sökandes doktorsavhandling (alternativt mastersuppsats) och andra vetenskapligt granskade publikationer. Purpose This internship focuses on biometric Presentation Attack Detection (PAD) using Vision-Language Models (VLMs), applied to face, fingerprint, iris and other biometric modalities. As identity spoofing techniques become increasingly sophisticated, fraud detection solutions must continuously evolve to ensure the reliability and security of biometric recognition systems. At the same time, the emergence of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), which combine visual information with textual descriptions, has opened up new opportunities for improving biometric presentation attack detection, including the detection of facial masks, video replay attacks and fake fingerprints. Integrating textual information into traditional visual-based approaches offers two main advantages: Improved detection performance: By leveraging large-scale semantic knowledge, VLMs go beyond simple pixel-level analysis, helping models focus on relevant visual cues and better distinguish genuine biometric traits from fraudulent attempts. Enhanced explainability: VLMs can provide natural-language descriptions of the visual cues behind their predictions, making detection results easier to interpret and supporting human review and validation. The objective of this internship is to investigate the state of the art in VLM-based approaches for biometric fraud detection, and then implement, adapt and improve the most promising methods. Key Missions Conduct a scientific literature review on Vision-Language Model (VLM) fine-tuning techniques, with a particular focus on their application to biometric Presentation Attack Detection Identify and select promising algorithms, then implement and adapt them to the targeted use cases Evaluate model performance, analyze results, identify limitations and explore potential improvements Profile & Other Information Education Final-year engineering student or Master's degree (M2) student specializing in Computer Vision, Image Processing or Deep Learning Technical Skills Strong knowledge of Computer Vision and Deep Learning Proficiency in Python and PyTorch Solid background in data analysis and software development Personal Skills & Languages Good command of written and spoken English, with the ability to read and understand scientific publications Good command of French Curious, proactive and self-motivated, with the ability to work independently Results-oriented, with strong analytical and problem-solving skills Good communication skills, with the ability to present ideas and findings clearly Strong interest in contributing to the full lifecycle of an algorithm, from design and implementation to integration, testing and optimization Internship Details Location: Osny, France Duration: 6 months Expected start date: 2027 By choosing to work at IDEMIA Public Security , you will join a unique tech company, offering a wide range of growth opportunities. It is the only player present simultaneously in five major luxury sectors : Wines & Sporits, Fashion & Leather Goods, Perfums & Cosmetics, Watches & Jewelry and Selective Retailing. The group currently employs more than 211,000 people worlwilde and generated revenue of 80,8 billion euros in 2025. About LVMH AI Factory The LVMH Data Science department, a global leader in luxury, designs and deploys cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence solutions for the Group’s Maisons. AI plays an ever-increasing role in personalization, efficiency, and innovation, all serving to enhance the client experience. Our work is guided by a “Human-Centered AI” approach, ensuring that our technologies are aligned with human values and the cultural specificities of our markets. Job Responsibilities Internship – Generative AI for Knitwear Design and Manufacturing Context Generative AI is already opening new creative directions in fashion design, particularly for image research, moodboards, and renderings. The Knit AI project explores the next frontier: extending this creative role all the way from an idea or reference image to a programmable, machine-made knitted object. Computerized flat-knitting machines execute ordered, symbolic, machine-readable instructions that specify operations such as knit, tuck, miss, transfer, racking, and yarn changes. These knit programs form a structured language that can be learned and generated by modern sequence models. The ambition is to investigate how AI can act as a creative collaborator, proposing novel and physically feasible knit structures, while preserving human expertise, judgment, and creative control. Objectives Design and test an end-to-end AI-assisted workflow from design intent to machine-compatible knit programs. Build a curated multimodal dataset pairing knit programs with renderings or 3D simulations, physical outcomes, and short design briefs. Train or fine-tune generative models able to propose candidate knit structures from text prompts or reference images. Define validation and evaluation protocols covering program validity, machine constraints, visual quality, technical feasibility, and creative relevance. Deliver a proof of concept and a roadmap for a broader research and industrialization phase. Missions Analyze the state of the art in inverse knitting, generative design, program synthesis, multimodal learning, and constrained generation. Work with knitwear design experts to collect, document, clean, and structure knit-program data, associated 3D simulations or renderings, physical swatches, and design briefs. Define a usable data model and transformation pipeline, including conversion to an intermediate machine-independent representation where relevant. Explore baseline approaches and train or fine-tune sequence or multimodal models to generate knit programs from prompts or images. Develop validity checks and constrained-generation methods so that proposed sequences comply with knitting grammar and machine constraints. Integrate generated programs into a digital knitting and 3D virtual-sampling workflow, then support the selection of candidates for physical prototyping. Evaluate outputs with both technical and creative criteria, documenting failure modes, model limitations, and opportunities for improvement. Produce reusable code, experiment documentation, a demonstration of the design-to-machine pipeline, and recommendations for the next phase. Expected Deliverables A curated and documented dataset pairing knit programs with visual outputs and design briefs. A reproducible data-processing and experimentation pipeline. A proof-of-concept generative model and a design-to-machine integration demo. A set of digitally simulated and, where feasible, physically knitted samples generated through the pipeline. An evaluation report covering technical validity, creative contribution, risks, limits, and a roadmap for a fuller phase. Profile Master’s degree in Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, or Data Science. Strong skills in applied mathematics and programming (Python, PyTorch/TensorFlow, etc.). Interest in applied AI challenges, research, and innovation. Ability to communicate complex topics clearly; excellent written and verbal communication skills in both French and English. Curiosity, rigor, and team spirit. Additional Information 5 to 6 month internship, starting from January 2027. Location: Paris 8th arrondissement, partial remote work possible. Supervision by the LVMH AI Factory team. Possible contribution to scientific publications or internal presentations.

items.desc:
Mission 
 The LIONS laboratory at EPFL, led by Prof. Volkan Cevher, is recruiting PhD students for ARC (Algorithms and Representations for Continual Learning), an ERC Advanced Grant project starting on January 1, 2027.
 ARC investigates how models can keep learning as their data and objectives change, while retaining useful capabilities and making better use of computation. Research will span optimization, representation learning, reinforcement learning, and game theory, connecting mathematical foundations with experiments on foundation models. More about ARC on CORDIS ( https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101267868) 
 Please note that to become a PhD candidate at LIONS and thus to be eligible for any of these positions, you must first apply to, and be admitted, into EDEE, EDIC, or EDRS. Applicants should follow the doctoral programs application instructions and list Professor Volkan Cevher as a potential host for their PhD studies. For more details please check: http://phd.epfl.ch/application.
 Profile 
 Master’s degree completed in computer science, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, statistics, or a related field.
 Strong foundations in one or more areas relevant to ARC, such as machine learning, optimization, representation learning, reinforcement learning, or game theory. 
 Interest in how machine learning models can adapt to changing data or objectives while retaining previously acquired capabilities. 
 Strong analytical or computational skills, with an interest in mathematical analysis, algorithm development, or experimental machine learning. 
 Evidence of research potential through a master’s thesis, research projects, internships, or publications. 
 Excellent written and spoken English. 
 Curiosity, initiative, and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team. 
 Main duties and responsibilities 
 Develop and carry out a doctoral research project within ARC. 
 Investigate methods for continual learning through mathematical analysis, algorithm development, or reproducible computational experiments, depending on the thesis topic. 
 Analyze research findings, prepare manuscripts for publication, and present results at conferences and workshops. 
 Collaborate with other ARC team members and contribute to discussions on shared research questions. 
 We offer 
 The opportunity to develop your own research ideas within ARC, an ERC Advanced Grant project on continual learning.
 A stimulating, international research environment in the LIONS laboratory at EPFL.
 A fully funded 4-year PhD position at EPFL, with salary according to the EPFL doctoral scale.
 Doctoral supervision and opportunities to collaborate with researchers, postdoctoral fellows, and fellow PhD students.
 The opportunity to pursue theoretical or experimental research and, where relevant to your thesis, connect mathematical ideas with experiments on foundation models. 
 Informations 
 Only applications submitted through the online platform are considered. You are asked to supply, in one PDF:
 A cover letter (one page) describing your motivation and relevant experience. 
 Your CV. 
 Transcript of your bachelor's and master's degrees 
 Contact details of at least two references.

 Contract Start Date : As of January 2027
 Activity Rate :100%

items.desc: About Pavo Pavo is building the Applied Science Factory: systems that develop an understanding of production ML, investigate performance, construct reliable evaluations, and help engineers make measurable improvements. We work with product behavior, code, data, models, and experiment history across real production systems. Our research covers training environments, scientific agent capabilities, and models for structured and behavioral data. We're a small team of researchers and engineers. Members of Technical Staff help define their research agenda and own the experiments, implementation, and evaluation end to end. The role You'll develop the datasets and reinforcement-learning environments used to train agents on applied-science tasks in production systems. The work includes executable simulations of user and product behavior, training tasks grounded in system dynamics, agent trajectories, and verifiers that check scientific conclusions. You'll study how environment fidelity, task diversity, data mixtures, and reward quality affect generalization to unfamiliar problems. You'll define the environment research agenda and own its implementation, evaluation, and integration with the model post-training loop. You'll work closely with the Scientific Capabilities owner, who is responsible for model-training recipes and capability gains. Design task distributions and curricula for diagnosing metric changes, investigating cohort effects, evaluating policies, and interpreting experiments. Implement agent tool APIs, sandboxed execution, deterministic reset/replay, rollout orchestration, trajectory versioning, and programmatic or statistical verifiers. Generate and curate synthetic data and expert/agent demonstrations; measure how data mixtures and environment diversity affect learning. Validate simulator behavior against known constraints and observed patterns; test reward exploits, data leakage, task difficulty, and transfer to held-out environments. What we look for Evidence of original technical work: an environment used for model training, a dataset or benchmark adopted by others, published research, or a substantial deployed simulation system. Grounding in probability, statistics, and experimental design; ability to represent interventions, observational bias, and delayed feedback. Experience testing verifier coverage and reward correctness, inspecting agent traces, and diagnosing environment or evaluation failures. Independent experimental judgment: strong baselines, controlled ablations, reproducibility, and ability to explain where simulated results transfer. items.desc: Phasecraft is the quantum algorithms company. We are building the mathematical foundations for quantum computing applications that solve real-world problems. Founded in 2019 by Toby Cubitt, Ashley Montanaro and John Morton, we are based in London and Bristol, UK. In 2023 we completed a £13m Series A funding round led by leading Silicon Valley deep tech VC, Playground Global. Phasecraft’s unprecedented access to today’s best quantum computers – through partnerships with Google, IBM, and Rigetti – provides us with unique opportunities to develop foundational IP, inform the development of next-generation quantum hardware, and accelerate commercialisation of high-value breakthroughs. Job Description Research Scientist — Audio Source Separation Description The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. Responsibilities Research, prototype, train, and evaluate novel source separation and extraction algorithms for speech and other real-world sounds. Develop approaches for single- and multi-microphone recordings, including spatial cues and optional auxiliary sensors. Investigate robust separation in challenging conditions such as overlapping talkers, noise, reverberation, and motion. Evaluate perceptual quality, separation performance, generalization, latency, memory, and computational requirements. Collaborate with DSP and embedded software teams to deploy models in real-time demonstrations and product platforms; contribute to patents and conference papers. Experience training and evaluating audio models in PyTorch; proficiency in Python and familiarity with C/C++ is a plus. Understanding of objective and perceptual evaluation methods and the tradeoffs involved in real-time low-power inference. Experience with multimodal or sensor-conditioned separation, ONNX/TFLite, or embedded deployment is a plus. Strong communication skills; publications at conferences such as ICASSP, Interspeech, NeurIPS, or similar are welcome but not required. The servicer platform (nicknamed WILL) and a set of client target objects will be filmed in flight. For post-mission analysis and simulation, the team needs an independent, high-accuracy record of how the target and the servicer moved relative to each other. You will build the vision system that produces it.
 Your role 
 You will own the Ground Truth Trajectory Reconstruction algorithm from design to flight data processing, and act as the technical champion of end-to-end testing on the engineering model (EM) hardware.
 Key responsibilities 
 Propose and justify a trajectory reconstruction strategy, in consultation with CVLab leadership (monocular vs. multi-view, marker-based vs. markerless vs. hybrid)
 Develop a visual odometry and pose estimation pipeline, adapted from open-source algorithms, that recovers the relative position and attitude trajectory of the target object and WILL from external viewpoint camera footage
 Define the optical marker surfaces and geometry requirements for the target objects and WILL
 Specify and oversee the manufacture of an optically representative target and WILL models
 Verify and validate the algorithm, and quantify accuracy, robustness, and failure modes under ISS-representative conditions (lighting and occlusion)
 Set up and lead end-to-end testing with EM hardware at the EPFL Space Center, covering the capture controller, grasper, and reconstruction chain working together
 Out of scope: hardware development and control algorithm development. You will integrate with and test against the controller and grasper, not design them.
 Required profile 
 Bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer vision, robotics, or a closely related field. A master’s degree is preferred .
 Demonstrated experience in visual odometry, SLAM, structure from motion, or 6-DoF pose estimation . Experience adapting and debugging existing open-source vision codebases (e.g. ORB-SLAM, COLMAP, OpenVSLAM or similar), is an asset.
 Solid working knowledge of multi-view geometry and camera calibration 
 Fluency in C++ and/or Python. 
 Ability to work with mechanical, GNC, and operations engineers and to explain vision results to non-specialists
 English fluency; working knowledge of French is an asset
 Desirable 
 Experience with fiducial markers , optical target design, or photogrammetry
 Experience with sensor fusion of vision and IMU data
 Experience with data from microgravity, space, or other harsh-imaging environments , or with space-qualified processes (ECSS, test documentation, review milestones)
 Familiarity with ROS or similar frameworks for hardware-in-the-loop testing
 Prior involvement in an ESA, NASA, or industry flight project
 Hands-on experience integrating software with physical test setups (cameras, IMUs, motion platforms, or similar hardware)
 A passion for the space sector!
 We offer 
 A stimulating and international working environment
 Excellent working conditions
 Opportunity to perform state-of-the-art research in one of the most dynamic scientific institutions in Europe.
 Opportunity to interact with internationally renowned experts, and with a strong team of postdoctoral researchers and PhD students
 An opportunity to have your work flown on the International Space Station! 
 Informations 
 Only applications submitted through the online platform are considered. You are asked to supply:
 A brief cover letter (pdf, up to 2 pages).
 And in one PDF :
 A CV with a publication list and/or relevant project experience.
Contact details for 3 referees.
 Where : EPFL Computer Vision Laboratory (CVLab), in collaboration with the EPFL Space Center
 Contract start date : mid February or March 1st, 2027
 Activity rate : 100%
 Contract type : CDD
 Duration : One year (extension subject to project outcome)

Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university. We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Overview Applications are invited for the post of Postdoctoral Research Associate (Ex Vivo Cancer) in the Ex Vivo Group, jointly led by Prof Sarah Danson (Clinical Lead) and Dr Greg Wells (Scientific Lead), within the School of Medicine and Population Health at the University of Sheffield. The Ex Vivo laboratory focuses on translational oncology and operates between the University of Sheffield and Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. The group screens drugs directly on patients’ cancer tissue as part of the observational clinical trial Ex Vivo Determined Cancer Therapy (EVIDENT), with the aim of predicting a patient’s response to treatment from a biopsy or surgical sample before treatment begins. The main role will involve establishing, optimising and running ex vivo cultures of patients’ tumour tissue, with a particular focus on tissues rich in extracellular matrix, such as breast and bone tissues. You will generate viable single-cell suspensions from dense, matrix-rich tissue for downstream processing and characterise cells through protein analysis, working closely with the group’s image analysis and bioinformatics team. Our ideal candidate will be an experienced cancer biologist with extensive hands-on expertise in primary human tissue culture and protein-based cell characterisation (e.g. Western blotting, immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence, flow cytometry), together with experience of working with clinical teams under Human Tissue Act governance. Main duties and responsibilities To work closely with other members of the Ex Vivo research group, including clinical, image analysis and bioinformatics colleagues, to develop and optimise the ex vivo screening project. To establish, optimise and maintain ex vivo cultures of patients’ tumour tissue from biopsy and surgical specimens, with a particular focus on tissues rich in extracellular matrix. To process and dissociate matrix-rich tumour tissue to generate viable single-cell suspensions for downstream processing, including flow cytometry, single-cell sequencing and cell culture. To characterise cells and tissues through protein analysis (e.g. Western blotting, immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence, flow cytometry and ELISA), and to prepare samples for imaging-based drug screening. To handle, store and record NHS-derived human tissue in line with the Human Tissue Act, research ethics approvals and the EVIDENT trial protocol. To attend and present at regularly scheduled laboratory meetings. To maintain accurate electronic records of all work carried out and all associated data records. items.desc: School of Engineering & Physical Sciences Location: Lincoln Salary: From £39,560 per annum Please note, this post is fixed-term and full time until the 28th February 2029 Closing Date: Tuesday 15 December 2026 Interview Date: Friday 08 January 2027 Reference: CHS359A Postdoctoral Research Associate in Medical Imaging AI for Brain Metastasis We are seeking an ambitious and collaborative Postdoctoral Research Associate to join a new EPSRC Health Technologies Connectivity Award led by Dr Wenting Duan at the University of Lincoln. The project focuses on developing clinically grounded AI for brain metastasis imaging in close collaboration with Professor Dorothee Auer and Dr Stefanie Thust, alongside clinical and imaging researchers at the University of Nottingham and Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust. This is an exciting opportunity for a talented early-career researcher to help shape a focused and growing research programme at the interface of artificial intelligence, medical image analysis, and clinical neuro-oncology. The project is motivated by real clinical challenges in brain metastasis imaging, including small and difficult-to-detect lesions, variation in MRI protocols across hospitals, lesion heterogeneity, and the need for robust and clinically meaningful methods that can translate beyond narrow benchmark settings. The successful candidate will work closely with the Project Lead and partner clinical collaborators to develop and evaluate AI methods for brain metastasis detection and analysis using public and partner imaging datasets. Depending on expertise and project needs, this may include work on lesion detection and segmentation, multimodal analysis, model robustness and generalisation, morphology-aware analysis, and clinically informed evaluation. The role will also involve dissemination through high-quality publications and conferences, engagement with external stakeholders, and contribution to the development of future translational funding opportunities. A distinctive feature of this post is the opportunity to work within a strongly interdisciplinary setting. The project is designed not only around technical AI development, but also around engagement with clinical workflow, imaging practice, and real translational constraints. The postholder will benefit from research visits to collaborators, access to computing support and research equipment, conference participation, and immersion in a collaborative clinical research environment. Applicants should have, or defended the viva of, a PhD in computer science, artificial intelligence, medical image analysis, biomedical engineering, or a closely related discipline. We are particularly interested in candidates with a strong technical background in medical image computing, machine learning, computer vision, or multimodal AI, together with excellent programming and communication skills. Experience in areas such as lesion detection or segmentation, domain generalisation, robust evaluation, clinically motivated AI, or imaging biomarker analysis would be especially valuable. Evidence of research potential through publications, software, or other high-quality outputs is essential. We particularly welcome applicants who are excited by interdisciplinary research, motivated by clinically relevant problems, and keen to work in close partnership with imaging and clinical collaborators. The role would suit a candidate who wants to combine methodological strength with real-world research impact and who is ready to contribute actively to a developing research direction with significant future potential. Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 2 years. Start date: 01/03/2027 Please include the contact details of one academic referee on the online application form and upload: a full curriculum vitae a cover letter explaining your suitability for the role a short research statement (maximum two pages) For more information about the position, please contact Dr Wenting Duan (wduan@lincoln.ac.uk).

The School The School of Computing an d Engineering (SCE) brings together expertise across computing, engineering and technology, with a strong focus on applied teaching, research and innovation. The School supports research that addresses real-world technological challenges and works with external partners to translate research outcomes into practical applications. This post will be based within the School's research environment, working with an academic project team on robotics, machine learning and cyber-security. The project is supported by the University's research and innovation infrastructure and has a clear focus on developing and validating practical technology. The successful candidate will contribute to a research project on independent monitoring of AI-driven industrial robots. The Role We are seeking a motivated Research Assistant to join a research project developing an independent monitoring system that checks whether a robot has physically moved as it was commanded. The project focuses on AI-driven collaborative robots in industrial settings. Working within the School of Computing and Engineering and under academic supervision, you will set up a collaborative robot arm with force/torque sensing and depth cameras, and adapt the monitoring software to contact-rich factory tasks such as insertion and fastening. You will run a controlled test campaign in the laboratory, covering emulated cyber attacks, mechanical faults and AI errors, and build a labelled physical dataset from the results. You will also benchmark the system against existing approaches and contribute to its testing, evaluation and documentation. The role is hands-on and laboratory-based, with opportunities to contribute to project reports, technical demonstrations and engagement with industry partners. This is a full-time, fixed-term appointment until 31 March 2027, based at the University of West London, with occasional travel to partner sites in the UK. The Person You will have a degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electronic/Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Machine Learning or a related subject, together with practical experience relevant to the role. You will have strong Python skills and experience of applied machine learning, particularly for anomaly detection, behavioural analysis or time-series data. Practical experience with robotics software such as ROS 2, and with sensors on a robot such as depth cameras or force/torque sensors, is essential. You will have good analytical, problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to work independently, manage tasks against project milestones and contribute effectively within a small research team. Experience with contact-rich manipulation or Franka robot arms, security testing or fault injection, and awareness of industrial robot safety or cyber security standards would be desirable. items.desc: Ready for a challenge? Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We're a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience. Whether it's a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe. About this role Join our Partner Algorithms team and help build the intelligence behind Just Eat's marketplace, powering personalised experiences for tens of millions of customers across 14 countries. This is your opportunity to deliver end-to-end machine learning solutions that directly impact customer engagement and order growth. We're building JET's recommendation systems, generating personalised carousels of restaurants to help people find their order right on the home page of the app. We're looking for someone who can live our behaviours of lead, deliver and care while bringing technical excellence and innovation. This role sits at the intersection of cutting-edge AI as we integrate, train and develop ML and generative models into a live production environment. Help us compute data at scale for millions of users to help people find the food they want. We need someone who can challenge assumptions, translate ambiguous business problems into elegant technical solutions, and ship production-quality ML systems that make a measurable difference to our customers and partners. Note: This role can be based in Bristol or London. These are some of the key components to the position: Work within a team on the development and deployment of ML/AI solutions including embedding models, fine-tuned LLMs, and ranking systems that drive engagement and orders while raising the bar for technical excellence. Apply generative AI and LLM techniques to personalisation challenges at scale, generating recommendations for millions of customers Own your results by designing, running and interpreting A/B experiments with statistical rigour, measuring real impact on business metrics and holding yourself accountable. Collaborate with ML engineers to productionise models, implementing MLOps best practices and maintaining monitored pipelines that deliver consistent value. Break down silos by translating complex business questions into clear modelling approaches and communicating results effectively to product and commercial stakeholders. Be determined to take end-to-end ownership of well-scoped workstreams, independently framing problems, choosing approaches, running experiments and presenting findings. Move fast by writing production-quality Python code and efficient SQL for data pipelines and analyses that can scale across our marketplace. Aim higher by staying current with advances in search, retrieval, recommendations and LLM applications, bringing fresh ideas to drive the vision forward. What will you bring to the team? Strong experimentation skills with ability to design and interpret A/B tests, reason about statistical significance, and understand the gap between offline and online performance. Production-grade Python coding abilities that go beyond notebooks, writing clean, testable code suitable for engineering workflows and collaboration with technical teams. Proficient SQL skills across complex data warehouses, including partitioning, window functions, and large-table joins, with focus on query efficiency and data quality. Excellent problem-framing and communication skills to translate ambiguous business questions into modelling approaches and explain technical results to non-technical stakeholders based on respect and mutual support. Self-starter attitude comfortable with autonomy and ambiguity, thriving in fast-paced environments where you can build rapidly, test rigorously and roll out successes at scale. Strong collaboration skills to work effectively with senior data scientists, ML engineers, product partners and commercial teams across different levels and functions. This role will involve a lot of learning from experienced senior data scientists and a great opportunity to develop your skillset. If you are missing any specific point but are enthusiastic about the space and have evidence of taking your own initiative to upskill then don’t hesitate to apply. Bonus skills that will help you excel: Hands-on expertise in search, retrieval and recommendation techniques including embedding-based approaches, learning-to-rank, and vector similarity search with measurable business impact. Practical experience applying LLMs in production environments, including prompt engineering, fine-tuning, structured output validation and assessing generative output quality. Familiarity with real-time data pipelines and streaming infrastructure. items.desc: Summary Location: Basel - Onsite This role will offer relocation assistance The Immunology Data Science and Molecular Pathology teams in Biomedical Research at Novartis work at the intersection of multi-omic spatial profiling, digital pathology, and advanced spatial & imaging AI models. We are recruiting a data scientist with deep expertise in spatial data analysis (imaging and/or spatial transcriptomics), experience with extracting biological insights from such data, and a strong interest in translational research. The role will apply AI models and develop analysis pipelines for spatial profiling data. The scientist will become part of a multidisciplinary team of pathologists, data scientists, technology experts, and drug discovery teams to generate and test hypotheses, identify pathogenic mechanisms, and help discover biomarkers and clinically relevant biological features. In addition to contributing to individual drug discovery programs, the scientist will help shape the organization's spatial biology and digital pathology strategy, ensuring that emerging technologies, data standards and analytical capabilities enable integrated, scalable and AI-ready approaches to understanding tissue biology. About The Role Key responsibilities: Design and contribute to spatial biology studies addressing biological and translational questions from drug discovery projects. Develop analysis approaches, best practices and computational pipelines for spatial profiling data, including multiplexed imaging and spatial transcriptomics. Modify and apply AI approaches to extract biologically meaningful insights from complex multimodal datasets. Support the onboarding, assessment, and use of spatial data analysis methods, platforms and databases. Stay current with advances in spatial profiling data analysis and AI modeling, propose and test new methods, work in close collaboration with data scientists to harmonize analytical approaches. Work closely with pathology and biology experts to ensure spatial findings are interpreted in their appropriate morphological and disease context. Support scientific publications and present at external and internal conferences. Requirements Ph.D. in Machine Learning, Computational Biology or related field. Candidates with MSc in Machine Learning, Computational Biology or related field, with 4+ years of relevant industry experience will also be considered. Experience with spatial transcriptomics, spatial proteomics, multiplex tissue imaging, digital pathology and/or related tissue-based technologies. Hands-on experience with common data analysis frameworks and data formats, and with standard image analysis tools used in pathology labs. Excellent programming skills both in python and R; openness to learning new tools and technologies; familiarity with models and harnesses for AI-assisted coding. Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to communicate complex data insights and recommendations to cross-functional teams. Demonstrated contribution to biological interpretation of spatial profiling data, including scientific publications and conferences. Rewards At Novartis, we’re committed to reimagining medicine together - and rewarding the people who make it happen. The rewards of being part of our team go far beyond base pay and incentives. We also offer a variety of competitive benefits in kind to help you thrive personally and professionally, such as insurance plans, retirement plans, wellbeing resources and global recognition programs. In addition, we provide flexible and hybrid working options, where possible, and a minimum of 14 weeks paid parental leave. items.desc: Company Description WEBCORE SOLUTIONS is a technology-focused company dedicated to designing and delivering advanced software and data-driven solutions for a variety of industries. The organization emphasizes innovation in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and automation to help clients improve efficiency and decision-making. Team members collaborate across disciplines to build scalable, reliable systems that solve complex business problems. WEBCORE SOLUTIONS values continuous learning, modern engineering practices, and a supportive environment for professional growth. Role Description The Artificial Intelligence Engineer will design, develop, and deploy AI models and systems that support business applications at WEBCORE SOLUTIONS. This full-time, on-site role is based in Pryluky and involves collaborating with software engineers, data scientists, and product teams to build and integrate AI solutions. Day-to-day responsibilities include developing and training machine learning models, implementing pattern recognition and neural network architectures, and working with natural language processing (NLP) techniques for real-world use cases. The engineer will also write clean, maintainable code, conduct model evaluation and optimization, document technical designs, and support production deployments and troubleshooting. Qualifications Strong foundation in Computer Science and Software Development, including algorithms, data structures, and modern programming languages (e.g., Python, Java, or C++). Hands-on experience with Neural Networks and Pattern Recognition, including model design, training, and evaluation using frameworks such as TensorFlow or PyTorch. Practical knowledge of Natural Language Processing (NLP), with experience applying techniques like text classification, entity recognition, or language modeling. Ability to work with data pipelines, model deployment, and integration of AI components into production systems, ideally in a cloud or distributed environment. Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate complex ideas clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Experience with version control, testing, and collaborative development workflows; familiarity with MLOps practices is an advantage. Interest in staying current with AI research, tools, and best practices and contributing to a culture of continuous improvement.

In France, you join its Engineering department, about 300 people, in the AI Applied Engineer chapter and the AI Engineer archetype. Activities & Responsibilities Who you work with Product Engineers build the application around the model; you own how the model behaves inside it. Context Engineers prepare the knowledge your agents retrieve, and Platform Engineers own the shared harness, runtime and model-serving infrastructure; you own the agent logic and behaviour that runs on it. With the AI Product Manager and the client's domain experts, you define what a good answer is and review results together. You review code with your peers and help newer colleagues. What You Do Build Machine learning applications, such as scoring or time series forecasting, with all the necessary steps: data wrangling, training loops, cross validation, evaluation, and deployment. Build LLM applications and agents: context design, tool calling, multi-step workflows. Design how agents use knowledge: retrieval queries, re-ranking, citations. Build evaluation sets and pipelines: reference answers, automated scoring, review by domain experts. Track answer quality in production and fix what degrades. Choose models by quality, cost and latency. Fine-tune or distil a smaller model when prompting is not enough. Add guardrails against wrong answers, data leaks and prompt injection. Process documents with LLMs: extraction, classification, summaries. Must-haves Required Skills You have built an application or agent that calls an LLM, and you can explain where it worked and where it failed. You write tested, maintainable code. You already use coding agents in your daily work and check what they produce. You measure AI output quality with test sets and metrics, and you know how to limit made-up answers, prompt injection and data leaks. You know what it takes to put an LLM application in production and keep it there: deployment, monitoring, cost and latency. You start from the business problem, not the model, and you can explain to non-engineers when AI is not the right tool. Bonus, Not Required Fine-tuning or distillation of language models. A background in machine learning or statistics, for example from data science. Agent frameworks or protocols such as MCP. Multimodal inputs: documents, images, speech. LLM observability tools: tracing, cost tracking. You don't need to tick every box to apply. If you match most must-haves and want to learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

items.desc: Contexte du poste : Nous recherchons une personne pour concevoir et évaluer des modèles capables de détecter des défauts ou de prévoir une dégradation d’équipement à partir de données industrielles. Vous définirez les conditions d’évaluation avec la production, la qualité ou la maintenance afin que les résultats restent interprétables sur le terrain. Les essais prendront en compte la variabilité des équipements et des conditions de mesure. Missions principales : Transformer un besoin qualité ou maintenance en objectif mesurable. Analyser les historiques de capteurs, les journaux de maintenance ou les images disponibles. Organiser l’annotation des défauts avec les spécialistes du procédé. Construire un modèle de référence et comparer plusieurs approches adaptées aux données. Prévenir les fuites de données par des découpages temporels ou par équipement. Fixer les seuils selon le coût des faux positifs et des défauts manqués. Valider les résultats sur des conditions de production distinctes. Définir les indicateurs de suivi après déploiement avec les équipes d’industrialisation. Examiner la disponibilité des signaux avant de fixer une cible de prédiction ou de détection. Comparer le modèle à une règle métier simple pour mesurer le gain opérationnel. Compétences techniques requises : Python et bibliothèques de machine learning telles que scikit-learn. Traitement de séries temporelles ou de données de vision industrielle. Évaluation sur données déséquilibrées et analyse des erreurs. Préparation de jeux d’entraînement et reproductibilité des expériences. Capacité à interpréter les résultats au regard d’un procédé industriel. Analyse exploratoire et identification des biais liés aux capteurs ou à l’annotation. Sélection de métriques adaptées au coût d’une erreur en production. Compétences complémentaires appréciées : PyTorch ou outils de vision par ordinateur. Déploiement de modèles sur site ou en périphérie. Connaissance des données d’un système de supervision ou d’un historien industriel. Expérience de validation sur plusieurs lignes, sites ou générations d’équipements. Profil recherché : Formation en mathématiques appliquées, informatique ou ingénierie ou expérience équivalente. Réalisation de projets de machine learning sur des données réelles. Capacité à échanger avec les spécialistes du procédé et à présenter les limites d’un modèle. Environnement de travail : Travail à l’interface entre données industrielles, expertise du procédé et déploiement des modèles. Pourquoi rejoindre ce projet ? Évaluer l’utilité d’un modèle sur des situations d’atelier. Travailler sur des données de production dont la qualité et la représentativité influencent directement les décisions. Type de contrat : CDI / prestation selon contexte Localisation : Île-de-France Disponibilité : À définir

Bij KickstartAI versnellen we de adoptie van AI in Nederland door te werken aan urgente maatschappelijke vraagstukken. Onze AI-projecten hebben directe impact op gezondheid, duurzaamheid en de kwaliteit van leven in Nederland. Jouw unieke rol in het Nederlandse AI-ecosysteem Als Machine Learning Engineer werk je samen met het team aan het oplossen van complexe problemen en draag je bij aan de adoptie van AI in Nederland door ML-oplossingen te ontwikkelen en implementeren bij onze partners. Je neemt eigenaarschap over je werk en weet hoe je ML-methoden creatief kunt aanpassen en toepassen op real-world uitdagingen. Je werkt nauw samen met Machine Learning Project Managers en engineers, zowel binnen KickstartAI als bij onze partnerbedrijven, om ervoor te zorgen dat je technische oplossingen bijdragen aan duurzame impact. Door je groeiende expertise kun je junior collega's begeleiden en draag je actief bij aan het verbeteren van de best practices binnen het team. Dit ga je doen als Machine Learning Engineer Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het ontwerpen, bouwen en onderhouden van schaalbare machine learning-oplossingen die aansluiten bij de behoeften van onze partners. Dit omvat de volledige levenscyclus van ML-projecten: van data engineering en modelontwikkeling tot experimenten, implementatie en monitoring. Daarnaast richt je je op het implementeren van MLOps-best practices en werk je aan projecten met directe maatschappelijke impact. Als onderdeel van projecten organiseer je of neem je deel aan 3-weken durende Challenges: sessies waarin ideeën snel worden omgezet in werkbare AI-oplossingen met engineers van onze partner bedrijven – geen vrijblijvende hackathon, maar een gestructureerd proces met een duidelijke impact. Door actief kennis te delen, draag je bij aan de adoptie van AI binnen onze partnerbedrijven en de bredere AI-community. Concreet ga je: Beheren van de volledige ML-levenscyclus: van data engineering en modelontwikkeling tot experimenten, implementatie en monitoring in productie. Implementeren van MLOps-best practices om betrouwbare en efficiënte ML-systemen op te zetten. Werken aan projecten met directe maatschappelijke impact binnen sectoren zoals gezondheidszorg, duurzaamheid en logistiek. Actief kennis delen binnen de AI-community en bijdragen aan de adoptie van AI bij partnerbedrijven. Dit zoeken wij Wij geloven dat een sterk team bestaat uit diverse achtergronden. Ervaring met Tensorflow/Pytorch, Kubernetes, Docker is een pre, maar nieuwsgierigheid en leergierigheid zijn belangrijker. Dit krijg je ervoor terug Bij KickstartAI krijg je een technisch uitdagende rol waarin je werkt aan AI-innovaties die Nederland versterken. items.desc: We are seeking a motivated and collaborative Research Associate in Computational Robotic Manufacturing to join the Digital Manufacturing Lab, School of Engineering, at The University of Manchester. You will develop computational robotic methods for additive manufacturing and soft robotics, focusing on optimised 3D-printed structures and toolpaths that account for manufacturing constraints. Preparing research publications, developing research objectives and contributing to funding proposals. Collaborating with academic colleagues and students, including supporting research projects and student research skills. Managing research activities, communicating technical findings and building internal and external research networks. We welcome candidates who bring diverse perspectives, experiences, and approaches to their work. About You We encourage applications from individuals with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. You should demonstrate: Essential Criteria A PhD (completed or nearing completion), or equivalent, in Mechanical Engineering or Industrial Engineering. Experience in C++ programming and mathematical formulation. Excellent communication, interpersonal, organisational and time-management skills. Experience of computational robotics, motion planning or intelligent mechatronics. Experience developing research proposals or external funding applications. Experience supervising or supporting student research projects. Ability to work independently and collaboratively, evaluate complex data and meet deadlines. Specialist knowledge of computational design, advanced manufacturing, intelligent mechatronics or robotics. Desirable Criteria A strong record of journal publications and experience presenting research findings. We value transferable skills and real-world experience as much as formal qualifications. Our benefits include (Grade 6): Generous employer pension contribution 29 days annual leave plus bank holidays and Christmas closure Ride to work and EV car schemes For more information, please see University of Manchester Benefits and Flexible and Hybrid Working. items.desc: Vous recherchez un emploi dans une entreprise internationale, dynamique et à la pointe de la technologie ? MAF RODA est un groupe international, spécialisé dans la conception et fabrication de projets clé en main de calibrage et de conditionnement destinés au secteur des fruits et légumes. La capacité de MAF RODA à innover grâce à une politique d’investissement en R&D ambitieuse (robotique d’emballage ; …), un réseau international et un service après–vente de proximité, fait de lui le leader mondial dans son secteur d’activité. Le groupe est actuellement représenté par 1300 salariés et une dizaine de sites de production dans le monde, dont 200 ingénieurs répartis sur 6 bureaux d’études, et un CA consolidé de 211000 K€. Dans le cadre d'un renforcement de nos équipes, nous recherchons pour notre siège basé à Montauban (Région Occitanie) un(e) : INGENIEUR VISION PAR ORDINATEUR ET ROBOTIQUE (C#/C++/Python) H/F Au sein de l'équipe R&D en robotique, vous contribuez au développement des systèmes de perception visuelle intégrés dans nos solutions de robotiques industrielles. Vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec le Lead Technique Senior sur des projets concrets alliant traitement d'image, intelligence artificielle et pilotage de robots. C'est un poste à forte composante technique, qui vous offre une exposition directe aux problématiques de vision en conditions réelles : contraintes de cadence, variabilité des produits et environnements industriels exigeants. Vos missions techniques principales couvrent : 1) L’implémentation de wrapper permettant la communication avec des caméras industrielles RGB/RGBD/IR/linéaires pour l’acquisition d’images ; 2) La construction de base de données d’images, l’entrainement, l'évaluation et le déploiement de modèles de deep learning adaptés aux contraintes d'inférence de nos systèmes embarqués. 3) Le développement et l'optimisation de pipelines de vision par ordinateur —prétraitement, détection, segmentation et tracking — indispensables aux phases de comptages, de suivi et d’orientation du fruit. 4) L’intégration de ces modules au sein des couches logicielles développées en C#, C++ et Python ; Au-delà de votre cœur de métier en vision, vous participez pleinement à la vie logicielle de l'équipe. Vous contribuez au développement de composants logiciels génériques comme par exemple l’implémentation de protocole de communication avec les équipements industriels et les interfaces de pilotage moteurs. Vous participez à la revue de code, et prenez part aux efforts collectifs d'amélioration du code existant. Votre profil : Vous êtes diplômé d'une école d'ingénieur ou d'un master en informatique, traitement du signal et de l’image ou domaine connexe, et justifiez de 2 à 4 ans d'expérience en vision par ordinateur (notamment avec OpenCV), acquise en environnement industriel, robotique ou embarqué. Vous maîtrisez les bibliothèques de référence du domaine — OpenCV, ITK, PyTorch ou TensorFlow — et avez une pratique solide de Python. Vous avez une bonne compréhension des architectures de deep learning appliquées à la vision : CNN, modèles de détection d'objets, transformers visuels. Vous développez en C# ou C++ pour la partie back (une connaissance du Rust est un plus) et avez des notions de Framework UI comme WPF et PyQt et n'êtes pas déstabilisé par la proximité avec des couches bas niveau. Vous évoluez indifféremment sous Windows et Linux. Curieux et rigoureux, vous aimez comprendre les problèmes en profondeur avant de les résoudre. Vous êtes à l'aise dans un environnement où les contraintes sont réelles — cadence, précision, robustesse — et savez faire preuve de pragmatisme pour livrer des solutions fiables. Vous appréciez travailler en équipe, recevoir des retours techniques et progresser dans un cadre structuré par des profils expérimentés. Dans le cadre de sa politique de diversité, Maf Roda Agrobotic étudie à compétences égales toutes candidatures dont celles de personnes en situation de handicap. Intéressement/participation + horaires variables + avantages CSE. Le poste est basé à Montauban (82) et nécessite potentiellement des déplacements en France et à l’étranger.

items.desc: Rejoignez la révolution technologique du véhicule autonome et connecté au sein de Valeo ! Leader mondial des aides à la conduite, Valeo réinvente la vie à bord du véhicule et révolutionne l’expérience de conduite. Des solutions de connectivité et de commande intérieure aux systèmes de détection, la division Valeo Brain du Groupe vise à rendre la mobilité plus sûre et plus intuitive. Le Valeo Mobility Tech Center basé à Créteil (94) est le siège de la Division Valeo Brain . Ce centre de Recherche & Développement regroupe 1180 collaborateurs autour de la conception de systèmes avancés d’assistance à la conduite (ADAS), de solutions de connectivité, d’interfaces homme machine et de systèmes de surveillance de l’habitacle. Après avoir obtenu des résultats prometteurs sur des approches mid-to-end, notre ambition est de passer à l'échelle supérieure : développer une architecture End-to-End (Données capteurs → Modèle d’IA → Action) robuste. En vous appuyant sur notre baseline inspirée de TerraTransfer, votre objectif sera de repousser les limites de performance actuelles. Ce stage offre une forte dimension scientifique et peut mener à une publication internationale. Vos Missions Le stage s'articulera autour de deux phases majeures : Recherche & État de l'art (SotA) : Étude approfondie des modèles end-to-end et du Reinforcement Learning (RL) appliqués à la conduite autonome. Exploration & Implémentation : Selon vos appétences, vous piloterez l'un des 4 axes stratégiques suivants : Axe 1 - Sim-to-Real : Améliorer le réalisme de la simulation via le 3D Gaussian Splatting. Axe 2 - Vision-Language-Action (VLA) : Exploiter les modèles VLM pour la prise de décision complexe. Axe 3 - Encodage & Distillation : Optimiser les encodeurs de données capteurs et la distillation de connaissances depuis un expert RL "teacher". Axe 4 - Dimension Temporelle : Intégrer une mémoire (implicite ou explicite) pour passer de l'action instantanée à la planification de trajectoires complètes. À Propos De Vous Formation : Étudiant(e) en dernière année d'école d'ingénieur ou Master 2 spécialisé en Intelligence Artificielle, Machine Learning, Robotique ou Mathématiques Appliquées. Technique : Excellente maîtrise de Python et des frameworks de Deep Learning (priorité à PyTorch). Théorie : Solides bases en Reinforcement Learning et/ou en Computer Vision. Les "Plus" : Une expérience préalable avec des outils de simulation de conduite. Soft Skills : Vous possédez un véritable esprit de chercheur, une grande autonomie et la capacité de traduire des concepts théoriques en implémentations algorithmiques performantes. Nos Avantages Présence d’un comité social & économique (CSE) : voyages, activités sociales et culturelles Remboursement transport à hauteur de 70% Pourquoi Valeo ? Pour rejoindre un leader technologique et industriel, pionnier français dans l’innovation automobile Pour une carrière dynamique avec des opportunités de CDI, de thèse ou de Volontariat International en Entreprise (Programme VIE) Pour contribuer au développement d’une mobilité plus propre, plus sûre et plus intelligente Valeo accorde une grande importance à la diversité, qu’elle soit culturelle, intergénérationnelle, de genre ou qu’elle concerne les personnes en situation de handicap.

items.desc: Description De L’entreprise Chez Quantum Surgical , nous sommes une entreprise spécialisée dans la robotique médicale et l'intelligence artificielle. Notre plateforme robotisée d'ablation percutanée, Epione® , est dédiée au traitement curatif et précoce des cancers. Nous proposons ainsi une nouvelle approche du traitement du cancer en uniformisant l'accès aux soins. Davantage de patients peuvent ainsi bénéficier de traitements innovants, mieux ciblés et moins invasifs. Plus de 1 800 patients ont déjà été traités à travers le monde. Nous faisons désormais partie du groupe Precision IO , qui intègre également NeuWave Medical . Notre ambition de transformer les normes de soins en matière d'ablation tumorale et d'oncologie interventionnelle grâce à l'innovation. Description Du Poste Au sein de l’équipe IA, vous participerez au développement de solutions de traitement d’images pour la plateforme robotique Epione et pour le dispositif d’ablation percutanée par micro-ondes NeuWave. Votre stage portera sur l’élaboration d’un module d’aide à la planification pour les procédures osseuses : vous identifierez les critères qui guident la planification, sélectionnerez une ou plusieurs méthodes candidates répondant aux besoins cliniques et aux contraintes de calcul (temps et ressources), puis vous les implémenterez et les évaluerez. Ce poste est basé à Montpellier. Vos Missions Seront Les Suivantes Recueillir et analyser le besoin clinique pour la planification de procédures osseuses avec Epione Réaliser un état de l’art des produits et des solutions académiques existants Définir et prioriser les approches à tester Constituer au minimum un jeu de données pour évaluer la pertinence des méthodes Implémenter une à deux approches Évaluer ces approches et restituer vos résultats à l’équipe Profil Recherché Requis Vous préparez un diplôme d’école d’Ingénieur·e ou un Master, avec une spécialisation en analyse et traitement d’images ou en intelligence artificielle. Vous avez de l’expérience en Python et avec les frameworks de deep learning (TensorFlow, PyTorch). Vous maîtrisez les principes du machine learning et du deep learning, notamment l’architecture des réseaux de neurones convolutifs. Vous avez de solides compétences en communication et en travail d’équipe. Vous maîtrisez l’anglais professionnel. Souhaitable Vous avez une première expérience du traitement d’images médicales et vous connaissez les formats d’imagerie médicale (par exemple DICOM). Travailler chez Quantum Surgical (Precision IO Group) c’est : Rejoindre une équipe multiculturelle talentueuse et créative, et participer à l’aventure technologique et humaine d’une entreprise en pleine ébullition. Partager nos valeurs d’innovation, d’esprit d’équipe et de culture du résultat. Relever des challenges techniques stimulants. Aussi, nous étudions avec intérêt toutes les candidatures sans distinction pouvant être liée à une caractéristique physique ou morale. items.desc: Since our founding, IDEMIA Public Security has been on a mission to unlock the world and make it safer through our cutting-edge identity technologies. Our technology leadership makes us the partner of choice for hundreds of governments and thousands of enterprises in over 180 countries, including some of the biggest and most influential brands in the world. In applying our unique expertise in biometrics and cryptography , we enable our clients to unlock simpler and safer ways to pay, connect, access, identify, travel and protect public places – at scale and in total security. Our teams work from 5 continents and speak 100+ different languages. We strongly believe that our diversity is a key driver of innovation and performance. Purpose Biometric Presentation Attack Detection (PAD) aims to distinguish genuine biometric traits, such as faces or fingerprints, from spoofed representations, such as photographs or masks. One of the key differences between a genuine biometric sample and a counterfeit one lies in the material properties of the object. In this internship, you will investigate how these properties can be estimated directly from images and videos, independently of the subject's identity. Your objective will be to design an algorithm capable of estimating the visual material properties of different objects appearing in a video sequence. These properties include parameters commonly used in computer graphics and rendering engines, such as diffuse and specular reflectance, emission, roughness and albedo. Key Missions Conduct a literature review to identify and understand the state of the art in material property estimation Generate synthetic video sequences using a rendering engine, together with corresponding material property annotations Design, implement and iteratively improve an algorithm for material property estimation Evaluate the algorithm's performance on both synthetic and real-world data Profile & Other Information Education Final-year engineering student or second-year Master's student (M2) specializing in Computer Vision, Image Processing or Deep Learning Technical Skills Strong knowledge of computer vision and deep learning Proficiency in Python and PyTorch Solid background in data analysis and software development Interpersonal Skills And Languages Good command of written and spoken English, including the ability to read and understand scientific papers Good command of French Curious, proactive and self-motivated, with the ability to work independently Results-driven, with a strong problem-solving mindset Good communication skills and the ability to present ideas clearly Strong interest in contributing to the full lifecycle of an algorithm, from design and implementation to integration, testing and optimization Internship details Location: Osny, France Duration: 6 months Expected Start Date: 2027 By choosing to work at IDEMIA Public Security , you will join a unique tech company, offering a wide range of growth opportunities. You will contribute to a safer world, collaborating with an international and global community. We value the diversity of our teams and welcome people from all walks of life, regardless of how they look, where they come from, who they love, or what they think. We deliver cutting edge, future proof innovation that reach the highest technological standards and we’re transforming, fast, to stay a leader in a world that’s changing fast, too. At IDEMIA Public Security , people can develop their expertise and feel a sense of ownership and empowerment, in a global environment, as part of a company with the ambition and the ability to change the world. items.card: You will use your deep physiological expertise to design challenging problems, set defensible ground truth from real experimental and clinical data, and find where AI systems succeed or fail. Your work will directly shape how frontier AI is measured in biology. 🎯 What You Will Do Design challenging, biologically meaningful evaluations that test AI agents' scientific reasoning in human physiology and disease.
items.desc: 🧬 AI Biologist, Human Physiology 📍 Fully Remote - UK or EU 🕒 Permanent, full time, $140K to $180K OTE plus equity 🧠 Build rigorous evaluations testing AI agents on human physiology problems 🧪 Human physiology: cardiovascular and systems physiology, AI for biology 🏢 Role Context A growing AI for biology company is building rigorous scientific evaluations that test whether AI agents can handle real biological workflows. This role sits in a science-first team of scientists and engineers, focused on human physiology and disease. You will use your deep physiological expertise to design challenging problems, set defensible ground truth from real experimental and clinical data, and find where AI systems succeed or fail. Your work will directly shape how frontier AI is measured in biology. 🎯 What You Will Do Design challenging, biologically meaningful evaluations that test AI agents' scientific reasoning in human physiology and disease. Identify and analyse cardiovascular and systems physiology data, including cardiac MRI, ECG and haemodynamic datasets. Work with clinical and cohort datasets such as UK Biobank and MIMIC to establish reliable ground truth. Assess experimental designs, biological mechanisms, data quality and alternative explanations to ensure scientific rigour. Investigate where AI agents succeed or fail at interpreting evidence and connecting physiological mechanisms. Collaborate closely with scientists and engineers, using AI-assisted research and coding tools to speed up delivery. Own each evaluation from problem definition through to defensible, evidence-based ground truth. ✅ What We're Looking For PhD, MD or equivalent research experience in human, integrative, cardiovascular or translational physiology, or endocrinology. Deep understanding of cardiovascular or systems physiology, including how organ systems interact in health and disease. Hands-on experience analysing cardiac MRI, ECG, haemodynamic, or clinical and cohort data such as UK Biobank or MIMIC. Strong track record of independent research, experimental design and interpretation of complex biological findings. Exceptional scientific reasoning, with the ability to form and evaluate mechanistic hypotheses. Ability to code your own scientific data analysis in Python or R. Familiarity with AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT, or willingness to build them into research workflows. Experience across multiple physiological systems, or integrating molecular, physiological and clinical data, is a plus.
