items.desc: You will join a team of researchers and hardware designers, and your responsibilities will include researching domain-specific AI accelerators and their implementation. Depending on the domain in question, you will need to tailor the architecture in order to optimise key metrics such as performance, latency, energy efficiency and silicon area. Your core responsibility will be the RTL design of hardware modules. This end-to-end process includes researching state-of-the-art solutions, defining requirements, specifying the architecture, implementing the RTL, and testing and verifying the results. Working in a collaborative research environment will enable you to interact closely with researchers from across the organisation. You will be expected to document your findings, participate in technical meetings and publish your work in scientific journals, as well as presenting it at international conferences. You will be part of a lean, agile team, and your input will directly influence the team's output and the overall direction of the research. Your Future Tasks Include Research, design and implement domain-specific AI accelerators in hardware, tailoring novel architectures to optimize for performance, latency, energy efficiency, or area. Contribute to the RTL design of hardware modules, covering the entire process from requirements definition and architectural specification to implementation. Test, verify, and troubleshoot hardware modules to ensure they perform optimally within their intended use case. Work closely with other researchers in a collaborative environment to align hardware design with project goals. Document research findings and maintain technical documentation for developed hardware modules. Present your findings through scientific publications and as talks in international conferences. Participate in customer meetings where you present your designs and ideas Contribute actively to a lean, agile team, providing input that directly influences the team's output and project direction. Your Profile Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related subject. Solid knowledge of digital design and RTL development using SystemVerilog, Verilog or VHDL. Understanding of computer architecture, specifically memory hierarchies, data paths, and interconnects. Experience or strong interest in AI/ML hardware, such as Neural Processing Units (NPUs), Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), or other domain-specific accelerators. Experience with hardware verification tools and simulation environments. Ability to translate high-level algorithmic requirements into efficient hardware implementations. Strong motivation, initiative and willingness to explore new architectural approaches in a research setting. Good communication and teamwork skills are essential, as is the ability to collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary research teams. Important Facts About SAL Diverse research activities with many technical challenges. State-of-the-art laboratory facilities and equipment. Location in the heart of Europe in Austria – relocation support for non-European nationalities. Internal and external training opportunities for career development. Family & children friendly - actively shaping the compatibility of family and career. “Vital4SAL” to promote a healthy workplace (e.g. SAL coaching pool, trainings on mental health, physical activities, healthy snacks, 24/7 accident insurance) € 4 per day meal allowance in restaurants or € 2 per working day in supermarkets. We offer competitive salaries and additional benefits based on your experience and qualifications. For this position, your minimum monthly salary starts with EUR 4.056, paid 14 times a year. At three locations (Graz, Villach, Linz), SAL is conducting research along the entire ESBS value chain in the areas of sensor systems, power electronics, intelligent wireless systems, microsystems and embedded systems to develop future-oriented solutions for industrial production, health, energy, mobility, safety and more. You will develop high-quality data science products and solutions for clients as well as assets for our internal data teams, focusing on modeling and working alongside the Data Engineering team. Additionally, you will present findings, recommendations, and provide consultation to stakeholders, both internal and clients.

You will build large-scale data and analytics solutions, handling complex problems and advanced client situations. You will also learn best practices in data and analytics development, including framework, responsibility model, high-quality code, data security, sustainability, and scalability. Working in collaborative teams with diverse skill sets, you will foster effective teamwork and learn from colleagues in a multicultural and creative environment. Staying up-to-date with the latest advancements in data science tools, techniques, and technologies, as well as participating in first-class learning programs, will be a key part of your development. You will also develop strong client-facing skills, including effective communication, problem-solving, and presentation abilities.
 You will work with other data scientists, data/ML engineers, designers, project managers, and business subject matter experts on interdisciplinary projects across various industry sectors to enable business ambitions with data and analytics.
 Our tech stack is diverse. While we advocate for using the right tools for the right task, we also consider the client’s current landscape and preferences. Often, we use Python, PySpark, TensorFlow, PyTorch, Databricks, SQL, Docker, and Kubernetes. We also leverage our own proprietary tools such as Kedro, CausalNex, and MLRun and we work on a regular basis with cloud service providers such as AWS, GCP, and Azure.

items.desc: ArcelorMittal is the world’s largest steel producer. We use the most innovative technologies to create the steels tomorrow’s world will be made of. Every day over 125,000 of our talented people, located in over 60 countries, push the boundaries of digitalization, and use advanced technologies to create a stronger, faster, and smarter world. To help make this possible, they know they can depend on the support and training that a company of our scope and scale can provide. Comprising 1,650 researchers spread across 14 Research Centres around the world, our Global R&D team aims to continuously improve the quality of steel and its manufacturing processes. This involves investigating and developing disruptive technologies, reducing the carbon footprint of steel, and optimizing costs while maintaining uncompromising quality. The team's strong multicultural diversity, with over 30 nationalities, offers international experience and makes it possible to meet global needs. The team working in the area focuses on executing research and development projects for the company's global mining portfolio. Collaborating with local production units, the team employs laboratory and pilot-scale equipment to optimize mining assets, particularly iron ore concentrate production, using a proactive approach to ensure continuous improvement in efficiency and sustainability. Your role You will be responsible for developing, coordinating and implementing research and development activities focused on process improvement, operational efficiency and technological innovation. The role requires a solid understanding of mineral processing, with particular emphasis on comminution and classification processes. The position involves planning, developing and supervising experimental activities at laboratory and pilot scales, including grinding, classification and mineral processing tests using different types of equipment and technologies, such as HPGR, grinding mills and classification systems, among others. This includes defining experimental procedures, coordinating test execution, monitoring equipment performance, analysing results and translating experimental findings into practical process improvement solutions. Knowledge of process modelling, simulation and data analysis is also important to support the development and optimization of mineral processing solutions. You will provide technical leadership for the Comminution / Classification cluster, coordinating activities and priorities, supporting project execution, contributing to the development of technical expertise within the team, and driving the continuous development of the cluster's capabilities, technologies and experimental resources in line with R&D and business priorities. An important part of the role involves matrix coordination of personnel involved in experimental activities, particularly technicians and operators, providing technical guidance, organizing laboratory work and ensuring the proper execution of tests. This also includes supporting knowledge transfer, developing team capabilities and promoting safe and efficient laboratory practices. The position requires close collaboration with other R&D areas, laboratory teams and technical specialists from different departments to develop and execute multidisciplinary projects. Effective communication, knowledge sharing and coordination with project stakeholders are essential to ensure alignment and successful project delivery. All activities must be conducted in compliance with safety, environmental and quality standards, contributing to the development of innovative, efficient and sustainable mineral processing solutions. Experience in laboratory and pilot-scale mineral processing work, including experimental design, execution, and process development. Experience in applied engineering or industrial environments, with exposure to troubleshooting, process improvement, and data-driven problem solving. Project management experience in technical or research activities, ensuring delivery within safety, environmental, and quality standards. Knowledge of mineral processing engineering, with solid experience in beneficiation, comminution, classification, and concentration processes. Strong knowledge of comminution and classification processes, particularly for technical cluster leadership, and experience in people management and team leadership, especially in coordinating teams involved in laboratory and experimental activities. Fluent in English. Ability to work in a multicultural and multidisciplinary environment. Strong problem-solving mindset with ability to support on-site and experimental process optimization activities. items.desc: Description de la future affectation Domaine Appui - Information scientifique et technique Type de contrat CDI Intitulé Chargé.e d'études bibliographiques, bibliométriques et sémantiques dans le contexte évolutif de l'IA Date de début 15/02/2026 Description du poste / de la mission Rattaché.e à la Direction générale déléguée à la recherche et à la stratégie (Dgdrs) du Cirad, la Délégation à l'information scientifique et à la science ouverte (DiscO) est un collectif de spécialistes de l'information scientifique et de l'édition composé de 26 personnes. La Délégation a pour principales missions : i) L'acquisition, la gestion et la mise à disposition d'information scientifique aux publics cibles internes et externes via des bibliothèques physiques et numériques ; ii) L'appui à la recherche (analyse de l'information, formation, bibliométrie), à la publication (articles, revues, ouvrages), ainsi qu'à la gestion et la diffusion des données de recherche ; iii) L'administration, l'alimentation et l'évolution de systèmes d'information scientifiques dédiés aux revues, à la production scientifique écrite, et aux données de la recherche du Cirad. L'articulation entre science ouverte, bibliométrie et IA dessine un nouveau paradigme pour l'évaluation et l’analyse de la production scientifique. Elle invite à une vigilance méthodologique : qualité des données sources, transparence des algorithmes, interprétation critique des résultats et maintien de l'expertise humaine. Au sein de l’équipe « Bibliographie, Bibliométrie et Sémantique », vous contribuerez à la production des analyses scientométriques en appui au pilotage scientifique et stratégique du Cirad (indicateurs institutionnels, multidisciplinarité, ...) en exploitant le potentiel des outils IA. Missions principales Bibliométrie et IA Prise en charge de la production d'analyses bibliométriques en appui au pilotage scientifique et stratégique du Cirad en mobilisant des outils d’IA. Consolidation des indicateurs de suivi des pratiques de science ouverte et à l'usage et l'optimisation d'outils ouverts de repérage, visualisation, exploitation et valorisation des publications et des données de recherche. Contribution à la production de notes de synthèse en réponse aux demandes institutionnelles. Contributions aux projets collectifs Appui aux projets d’IA de la DGD-RS, en particulier pour l’analyse sémantique de corpus de documents. Accompagnement pour l'évolution de l'archive ouverte Agritrop en appliquant des techniques d'IA pour l'indexation et la recherche d'information. Appui méthodologique et opérationnel pour la production de méta-analyses actualisées et assistées par IA à la demande des unités et projets de recherche en collaboration avec les partenaires du Sud. Rédaction et formation Contribution à la rédaction des procédures et recommandations sur l’usage de l’IA. Participation à l’organisation d’ateliers de sensibilisation et de formation dans ce domaine en lien avec les missions de la DiscO. Accompagnent à la montée en compétence des collègues de votre service. Pour l'ensemble de vos activités, vous interagirez auprès de nombreux interlocuteurs internes (DiscO, autres services d’appui, collectifs scientifiques) et externes. Profil souhaité Vous détenez un diplôme dans les métiers de la documentation ou des sciences de l’information et des bibliothèques (niveau master). Vous avez une bonne connaissance de l’environnement du numérique et des recommandations pour la science ouverte, ainsi que des différents enjeux liés au développement de la bibliométrie (usages scientifiques et aide à la décision) et des nouvelles tendances (open citations, multidisciplinarité...). Compétences recherchées : Expérience dans le domaine de la scientométrie et connaissance de bases de données de publications ; Connaissance des différents enjeux liés au développement de la bibliométrie (usages scientifiques et aide à la décision) ; Une connaissance de la programmation informatique dans plusieurs langages (R et Python en particulier) serait appréciée La connaissance d'outils d'extractions d'informations (interrogation et exploitation des API de bases bibliographiques ouvertes : OpenAlex, Crossref, Unpaywall, Semantic Scholar, DataCite, OpenCitations …) La connaissance des outils d'analyses réseaux et sémantiques (Cortex, Gephi, Gargantex, VosViewer) serait un plus ; Compétences pédagogiques, capacité à transmettre pour accompagner l'évolution de compétences. items.desc: Xsensio SA is looking for an experienced scientist or engineer to build, from the ground up, a dual-biomarker sensing platform for preeclampsia and to integrate it into microneedles for measurements in interstitial fluid (ISF). You will own the full development path: bioreceptor selection, surface chemistry, electrochemical detection, analytical validation and miniaturization. Location: Lausanne, Switzerland · Contract: 1 year, renewable, 100% · Start date: January 1st, 2027 THE PROJECT Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality worldwide. The ratio of two circulating proteins, soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1) and placental growth factor (PlGF), is an established tool for assessing preeclampsia risk, but today it requires a blood draw and a central laboratory. Our project, funded by a major global health foundation, aims to make this measurement accessible through a minimally invasive microneedle sensor that detects both biomarkers in ISF. The project builds on Xsensio's existing modular biochemical sensing platforms. YOUR ROLE You will lead the sensor development independently, from concept to an integrated microneedle demonstrator: Define the detection strategy. Review the state of the art and select the transduction method. Select and qualify bioreceptors for sFlt-1 and PlGF, including affinity, kinetics and cross-reactivity. Develop the surface chemistry: receptor immobilization, blocking and antifouling layers that keep the sensor working in a protein-rich matrix. Build the dual-biomarker assay and manage cross-talk between the two detection channels. Validate analytically: limit of detection, dynamic range, selectivity, reproducibility and stability, benchmarked against a reference method such as ELISA. Miniaturize and integrate the sensor into microneedles, working with our microfabrication and electronics colleagues to transfer the assay from macro electrodes to microelectrodes. Report and communicate: document results for the funder, present to project partners, and contribute to publications and intellectual property. YOUR PROFILE PhD in biochemistry, bioengineering, analytical chemistry, electrochemistry or a related field. Postdoctoral or industrial R&D experience is a strong plus. A track record of developing affinity-based biosensors or immunoassays for protein biomarkers, ideally from scratch and at low concentrations (pg/mL to ng/mL). Hands-on expertise in electrochemical techniques: EIS (faradaic and non-faradaic, including equivalent-circuit modelling), cyclic voltammetry, and differential pulse or square wave voltammetry. Solid experience in surface functionalization and bioconjugation: self-assembled monolayers on gold, EDC/NHS and related coupling chemistries, and antifouling strategies. Experience characterizing biomolecular interactions and functionalized surfaces with several of the following: SPR, BLI or QCM-D for binding kinetics; ELISA as a reference assay; XPS, contact angle, AFM, SEM or fluorescence microscopy for surface analysis. Rigour in analytical validation: calibration, limit of detection and quantification, selectivity and interference studies, matrix effects, statistics. Proven ability to work independently, structure a development plan and deliver against milestones. Fluent written and spoken English. NICE TO HAVE Experience with microelectrodes, microneedles or wearable sensors, and with the effects of miniaturization on electrochemical signals. Work in complex biological matrices (ISF, serum, sweat) and continuous or reagent-free sensing formats. Multiplexed electrochemical detection. Data analysis in Python, MATLAB or similar. WHAT WE OFFER Technical ownership of a new sensing platform, with the freedom to shape the approach from day one. A project with direct relevance to maternal health, supported by the foundation. A multidisciplinary environment covering microfabrication, system integration, electrochemical sensing and electronics. Access to state-of-the-art research equipment offered by EPFL. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

items.desc: About the Role Launch your career at the forefront of measurement science At NPL, you'll use science and engineering to solve complex real-world challenges, working alongside leading experts to develop the measurements, standards and technologies that underpin innovation across the UK. Why join NPL’s Graduate Programme? As a Graduate Scientist, you'll join one of our scientific teams and contribute to meaningful projects from day one. NPL's work spans a broad spectrum, from fundamental research and technology development through to measurement services, industrial collaborations and customer-focused scientific projects. Throughout the programme, you'll gain experience of how scientific expertise is applied in different ways to deliver impact for industry, government and society. This two-year programme includes two rotational placements, giving you the opportunity to experience different areas of NPL, broaden your technical expertise and develop a deeper understanding of how measurement science supports innovation across a range of sectors and applications. You will be based at our Teddington site and while working alongside experienced scientists and engineers, you'll develop your expertise through hands-on experimental, analytical and technical work. Whether you're supporting cutting-edge research, developing software and technical capabilities, delivering measurement services, solving customer challenges or contributing to the development of new opportunities and capabilities, you'll play an important role in advancing science that makes a real-world difference. You'll benefit from a structured professional development programme covering communication and presentation skills, project management, commercial awareness, strategic thinking and personal effectiveness. These skills will complement your technical development and help you succeed in a collaborative, customer-focused scientific environment. You will also be involved in supporting our community benefit activities – this may be going to local schools, supporting Outreach or helping at large NPL events. We will provide you with the opportunity to be part of a caring and daring community that truly values you and your contribution. What could you work on? Graduate rotational placements are expected to be available across the following scientific teams and disciplines. To learn more about each area and explore some of the projects, capabilities and technologies involved, follow the links below: Advanced Engineering Materials : Investigating the properties and performance of materials used across various sectors including aerospace, manufacturing, energy and emerging technologies, helping organisations develop products and processes that are reliable, safe and fit for purpose. Data Science and AI Applying advanced analytics, informatics, machine learning and artificial intelligence to complex scientific datasets, helping transform measurement data into actionable insight, improve scientific processes and accelerate innovation across NPL. Understanding how the structure, lifecycle and overall quality of data affects confidence in making decisions. Gas Metrology Developing highly accurate measurements for gases that support air quality monitoring, emissions measurement, clean energy technologies and the transition to net zero. Emissions and Atmospheric Metrology Creating and improving the measurement methods and standards used to monitor our environment, supporting measures to address air quality, pollution, and greenhouse gases, providing confidence in data used to understand and manage environmental change. Life Sciences, Health & Bioeconomy: NiCE MSI (National Innovation Centre for Excellence in Mass Spectrometry Imaging) Developing advanced imaging and analytical techniques that provide detailed insight into biological samples and materials, supporting progress in healthcare, pharmaceuticals and biomedical research. Biometrology Developing the measurement methods, standards and tools that underpin reliable and reproducible biological and life sciences research. Ultrasound and Underwater Acoustics Supporting the development and application of acoustic measurement techniques used in healthcare, marine monitoring and underwater technologies. items.desc: Are you excited by the potential of foundation models to transform how we understand places and the people who move through them? Would you like to help build a new generation of geographic models grounded in how people actually perceive and remember cities? Do you enjoy working at the boundary between machine learning and real-world application? ReCoGNiSe (Representations of Cognitive Geography for Navigating Sustainable Neighbourhoods) is a five-year, €2m research programme funded by a European Research Council Consolidator Grant. ReCoGNiSe starts from a critical disconnect at the heart of geographic analysis: that the digital representations of space on which spatial data are built do not reflect how places are perceived and remembered. The project aims to initiate a step-change in how geographic space is represented, building new representations of spatial features and relations, grounded in spatial cognition and computational neuroscience. We are looking to recruit a passionate researcher to lead our work on cognitive feature representations using foundation models. You will use a vast array of data to build rich, multimodal representations of urban cognitive features, capturing facets such as visual salience, cultural significance, function, and locational importance. This will involve working with general-purpose language, vision-language and multimodal models, alongside geospatial foundation models. Your representations will provide the foundation for the project's cognitive map representations. Working with the wider project team, you will adapt approaches to reflect newly collected data on how features are perceived differently across populations and over time, and integrate with other work on constructing models of spatial learning. They will also underpin the project's open-source releases. Candidates will require expertise in deep learning and foundation models, ideally applied to geospatial or human-generated data. Given this work sits at the interface of GeoAI, geography and neuroscience, we are particularly seeking applicants who enjoy working across disciplinary boundaries, are committed to open and responsible AI, and are keen to engage with theory from geography and spatial cognition. This role will be hosted within the Mobility Science Lab, in the Institute for Spatial Data Science (ISDS) at the School of Geography. As well as working closely with Prof Ed Manley and the wider ReCoGNiSe research team (totalling three Research Fellows and two PhD students), you will collaborate with Dr Weiming Huang (University of Leeds), who brings expertise in foundation models and GeoAI, and Prof Hugo Spiers (UCL), who brings expertise in the neuroscience of spatial cognition. You will also benefit from the project's international network of collaborators in spatial cognition, GeoAI and urban science. To discuss the post further or for any queries you may have, please contact: Ed Manley , Professor of Urban Analytics - Email: E.J.Manley@Leeds.ac.uk

Branchenführenden Kooperationen in den Bereichen Cloud, BI und AutoML Arbeit in einer offenen, flachen Umgebung, innerhalb eines breiten Reply-Netzwerks zum Wissensaustausch Preisgekrönte Büroräume in der Münchner Innenstadt mit Zugang zur Stammstrecke Fahrkarte für öffentliche Verkehrsmittel mit Deutschlandticket Zuschuss zu einer Fitnessstudio-Mitgliedschaft in einem Fitnessstudio der Wahl oder die Nutzung von Wellpass Flexible Arbeitsumgebung zwischen Kunden, Reply-Büro und Remote-Arbeit Über Machine Learning Reply Machine Learning Reply bietet maßgeschneiderte End-to-End-Lösungen im Data-Science-Bereich an, die den gesamten Projektlebenszyklus abdecken – von der initialen Strategieberatung über die Datenarchitektur und Infrastrukturthemen bis hin zur Datenverarbeitung und Qualitätssicherung unter Verwendung von Machine-Learning-Algorithmen. Machine Learning Reply verfügt über umfassende Expertise im Bereich der Datenwissenschaft in allen Schlüsselindustrien der deutschen HDAX-Unternehmen. Machine Learning Reply befähigt seine Kunden, neue datenbasierte Geschäftsmodelle erfolgreich einzuführen sowie bereits bestehende Prozesse und Produkte zu optimieren – mit einem Schwerpunkt auf Open-Source- und Cloud-Technologien. Mit dem Machine Learning Incubator bietet das Unternehmen ein Programm zur Ausbildung der nächsten Generation von Entscheidungsträgern, Data Scientists und Entwicklern an. Wir freuen uns auf deinen Studienabschluss mit einem quantitativen oder wirtschaftlichen Hintergrund, zum Beispiel in Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Wirtschaftsmathematik oder Betriebswirtschaftslehre Mit deiner einschlägigen Erfahrung in Datenwissenschaft & Datenmanagement oder der Entwicklung von Produktionssystemen verfügst du über gute Kenntnisse in Python, R, Rust, Pyspark oder SQL Mit den Grundlagen der Statistik und des Machine Learning bist du vertraut und kennst auch deren Anwendungen in der Produktion wie NLP, Recommender-Systeme, Time Series Analysis und Computer Vision Außerdem bist du vertraut mit Cloud-Plattformen wie AWS, Google Cloud oder Microsoft Azure Auf Deutsch und Englisch kommunizierst du gut und gerne Du bist lernbereit, teamfähig und kannst technische Konzepte verständlich kommunizieren Du hast gute Projektmanagementfähigkeiten und kannst sowohl unabhängig als auch im Team arbeiten

items.desc: Data Scientist Who we are VIRTHIO is a technology consulting company working with national and international clients across multiple industries, including Banking, Services, and Energy. We help organizations address their technological challenges by connecting them with specialized IT professionals and delivering tailored solutions. Our expertise spans IT Consulting, Nearshore, Turnkey Projects, Blockchain, Machine Learning, and other technology-driven areas. What you will be doing Explore and process complex datasets to uncover relevant insights and identify opportunities for business improvement; Build and refine Machine Learning models to solve real-world problems and support data-driven decision-making; Prepare and transform data through feature engineering and feature selection techniques; Assess model performance, conduct experiments, and fine-tune algorithms to improve accuracy and reliability; Develop workflows to support model training, testing, and deployment; Work alongside Data Engineers to ensure data availability, quality, and suitability for analytical projects; Support the deployment and ongoing monitoring of models, contributing to reliable and scalable ML solutions; Apply MLOps/LLMOps principles to improve automation and manage the Machine Learning lifecycle; Present findings and translate technical results into practical recommendations for business stakeholders. What you will need to succeed Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, or a related technical field; Experience working in Data Science and Machine Learning; Practical experience developing and evaluating Machine Learning models, ideally covering the full lifecycle through to deployment; Proficiency in Python and SQL; Knowledge of feature engineering, model validation, and hyperparameter optimization; Familiarity with cloud environments such as AWS, Azure, or GCP; Understanding of model deployment, monitoring, and MLOps practices is an advantage; Strong analytical thinking and the ability to approach business challenges through data; Good communication skills and the ability to collaborate with multidisciplinary teams; Autonomy, adaptability, and willingness to learn new tools and technologies. What the company will offer you An open-minded company that values initiative, independent thinking, and each team member’s contribution; A collaborative environment with opportunities to exchange knowledge and develop new skills; Career development and continuous learning opportunities; A hybrid working model, with the role preferably based in Porto; The opportunity to contribute to innovative projects involving Data Science, Machine Learning, and advanced analytics. Next Steps If you are interested in this opportunity, we would appreciate it if you could share your updated CV with us at bernardo.miranda@virth.io . Alternatively, if you are looking for new professional challenges, feel free to get in touch — we will be happy to discuss other career opportunities with you.

items.desc: Responsibilities The livestream industry has seen tremendous growth in recent years and has become the next growth driver for TikTok global business. It also brings great joy to users globally and it creates a new channel for our creators to show themselves. We are seeking an AI Data Operation Specialist to join our team to lead quality initiatives in content moderation—leveraging both human labeling and machine learning models, including Large Language Models (LLMs). This role plays a critical part in upholding content quality across TikTok Live platform. The ideal candidate will be deeply involved in training AI models, analyzing moderation data to extract actionable insights, resolving complex content scenarios, and working closely with partner teams to ensure effective issue resolution. Success in this role requires strong analytical thinking, high ownership, and the ability to collaborate across cross-functional teams. A keen eye for detail and a proactive mindset toward challenging existing processes and driving continuous improvement are essential. Detailed responsibilities include: - Ensure high-quality content benchmarking across BPO teams, support the setup, onboarding, and training of new BPO teams. Manage policy clarifications, calibrations, and arbitration processes. Analyze BPO team performance to identify knowledge gaps and systemic issues. - Handle content labeling for specific queues based on cross-functional business requirements, analyze labeled content to identify trends and provide insights to project teams and independently manage quality evaluation initiatives, delivering actionable analytical insights. - Train models using large datasets of labeled content to improve decision-making accuracy. Enhance model capabilities through iterative training and reinforcement learning, assist in data preparation, cleaning, and structuring for training purposes. Improve model accuracy by testing and fine-tuning, highlight the algorithm team with supporting examples for any potential gaps in LLM decision making draft, revise, and quality-check content to explore and enhance the synergy between human input and data in LLM training. - Analyze moderation and labeling data from multiple queues to derive a process or market specific trend/correlation. Arrange supporting data points for impact analysis and solution planning. - Custodian of all quality specific artifacts for the content moderation scope, generating creative solutions, including the use of technology and tools, to enhance the quality of both individual and team outputs. Qualifications Minimum Qualification(s): - Bachelor’s degree in Business, Data Science, Computer Science, Information Technology, Communications, or a related field - 3+ years of experience in AI data operation, leveraging AI and ML for content quality management, product operations, or a related analytics role - Proficiency in data analysis and visualization tools such as Excel, Tableau, Power BI, or similar - Basic understanding of machine learning concepts and Large Language Models (LLMs) - Strong ability to analyze complex datasets, identify patterns, and generate actionable insights - Fluency in both written and spoken English is essential as it will be utilized as the primary language for daily work. In addition, to better understand live streaming content in specific regions and better monitor and improve the ecosystem health of the French markets, proficiency in French is also necessary. Preferred Qualification(s): - Prior experience in tech, digital content, or platform moderation environments - Able to review and analyze potentially disturbing content with objectivity, professionalism, and emotional resilience - Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate data into actionable insights, influence strategy, and drive impactful solutions - Highly adaptable, proactive, and self-motivated, with a proven ability to thrive in fast-paced and constantly evolving environments - Solid understanding of machine learning principles, including model evaluation metrics and optimization techniques - A deep interest in LLMs, human behavior and user experience is essential. The ideal candidate is an enthusiastic learner who finds engagement with diverse case studies and annotators stimulating - Experience as RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) annotators for leading AI/LLM companies is strongly preferred About TikTok TikTok is the leading destination for short-form mobile video. At TikTok, our mission is to inspire creativity and bring joy. TikTok's global headquarters are in Los Angeles and Singapore, and we also have offices in New York City, London, Dublin, Paris, Berlin, Dubai, Jakarta, Seoul, and Tokyo.​ Why Join Us Inspiring creativity is at the core of TikTok's mission. Our innovative product is built to help people authentically express themselves, discover and connect – and our global, diverse teams make that possible. Together, we create value for …

items.desc: To start as soon as possible | 6-9 months| Rotterdam Internship: Machine learning - Imitation learning and the effect of force feedback Send application Position Overview The SenseGlove R1 is a glove with force feedback, with the goal of achieving lower forces during imitation learning. We want to investigate under which conditions it can help or hurt the machine learning outcomes. The main focus of this internship is developing imitation learning that benefits the most from the glove’s force feedback, both with a real robot arm and robot hands, and in simulation. This allows us to advise customers on the best setup and provide a starting point for them to build on. We are looking for an ambitious student who wants to do cutting-edge research, likes to push through difficult problems, and wants to publish a paper in a recognized journal as the outcome. Thesis only, or a combined internship and thesis. Build and maintain the release process for models: rollout, rollback, bringing up new pods, versioning of models and serving configs. Move our GPU workloads from Nomad to Kubernetes. Cluster setup, networking and security are
items.desc: TLDR: We’re looking for an MLE / MLOps Engineer to own how our models get to production and stay there: GPU Kubernetes, releases and rollbacks, observability, and turning research prototypes into services people can rely on (roughly half infra, half delivery). About Us White Circle is an AI Safety company building the safety, reliability, and optimization layer for AI systems. At the core of our platform are policies – simple natural-language rules that define what an AI model should and shouldn't do. We automatically test, enforce, and continuously improve these policies at scale. We've raised $11M from top funds, founders, and senior leaders at OpenAI, Anthropic, HuggingFace, Mistral, DeepMind, Datadog, Sentry, and others We process over one hundred million API calls every month We fine-tune and train our own LLMs so they run faster and cheaper than any open or proprietary model What you'll do Deploy models from the research team to production and own those deployments end-to-end, including shadow evaluation and canary rollouts before a model takes full traffic. Build and maintain the release process for models: rollout, rollback, bringing up new pods, versioning of models and serving configs. Move our GPU workloads from Nomad to Kubernetes. Cluster setup, networking and security are already covered. Your part is the GPU layer: scheduling, autoscaling, NVIDIA drivers and device plugins, and an API researchers use to submit jobs. Own observability and reliability of our GPU services: metrics, dashboards and alerts for latency, throughput, queue depth and GPU utilization, and incident investigation when those numbers move. Develop and maintain internal services and pipelines that begin as research prototypes, such as data labeling and policy discovery. This is hands-on software engineering and makes up about half of the role. Maintain the environment researchers run experiments in: Kubernetes with the relevant plugins, SageMaker where it fits. Who you are 3+ years running ML systems in production, GPU workloads in particular Strong Kubernetes. You’ve operated GPU nodes and know what breaks between the driver, the runtime and the container Comfortable with Prometheus, PromQL and Grafana. You can read the logs and metrics of an inference service and say what’s wrong You’ve built release pipelines with canaries and rollbacks, and used them under pressure You write code well enough to take someone else’s prototype and turn it into a service you’d be happy to be paged for You’d rather ship and run models than research and train them. You like finishing things more than starting them A plus: hands-on experience with vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT or TensorZero, a Nomad-to-Kubernetes migration behind you, GPU autoscalers and job schedulers. Compensation & Benefits Competitive compensation, including equity Flexible time off Office in central London/Paris with flexible hybrid setup Relocation support if you’re moving to Paris, available after your probationary period Premium private health insurance Mental health support, including coverage for therapy when you need it Quarterly sports allowance for the gym, classes, or whatever keeps you active Lunch and dinner covered when you work from the office Learning and development support for courses, conferences, and opportunities to grow your skills All the hardware, subscriptions, tools, and services you need Team off-sites twice a year: we’ve recently been to the Alps, Saint-Tropez, and Marbella How we hire Intro call with Talent Take-home assignment Technical interview with DevOps Engineer Technical interview with Head of Engineering and Head of Applied Research Final call with CEO Compensation Range: $100K - $150K

This is a contract role for a self-starting engineer who can understand a problem, shape the architecture and independently deliver a tested, working solution. You’ll operate across full-stack engineering, AI systems, architecture and customer delivery , translating real-world requirements into robust production software. A major focus will be using Cursor, Codex and AI-assisted development tools to accelerate delivery while maintaining high standards around code quality, testing and reliability. You’ll take ownership from requirements through architecture, development, testing and production deployment. This includes building containerised services with Docker , APIs, distributed systems, event-driven pipelines and AI-powered applications. We’re looking for strong full-stack engineers with experience shipping real production software. Relevant technologies include Python, FastAPI, Docker, GitHub Actions, Azure, AMQP, PyTorch, OpenCV, CUDA, OCR, embeddings, LLMs and VLMs . You must be self-starting and client-facing , comfortable working directly with customers and reseller partners, understanding complex product requirements and then going away, building, testing and delivering a solution that works in production. Engagement: Perm | Focus: Full Stack / AI / FDE / Production Engineering

items.desc: About Act There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting. Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting. items.desc: ML Inference Engineer (GPU Performance) Make in-house models fast and cheap enough to run in production. Large models are expensive to serve well. When users expect fast responses, latency, throughput and cost per token decide whether the product feels usable. You'll join an early-stage AI lab that trains its own models and serves them in its own production AI products. Inference engineers here work closely with research, so serving performance feeds into how models are designed, not only how they're deployed. The opportunity You'll work on the serving stack behind the lab's models, getting more out of every GPU so users get fast responses at a sensible cost. This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll go from reading new inference papers to writing kernels and shipping the improvements to production. Your focus: Build and scale serving pipelines with tight targets on latency and cost. Reduce memory use and raise throughput through quantisation, compression, caching and distributed serving. Write custom GPU kernels for the hot paths, from attention to large matrix multiplications. Work with researchers on architecture choices so models are efficient to serve from the start. Follow new work on attention, KV cache management and batching, decide what's worth adopting and implement it. What you'll bring An MS or PhD in computer science, machine learning or a related field. Strong production code in Python, C/C++ or Rust. Hands-on GPU programming experience with CUDA, Triton or Metal. Practical experience with quantisation and model compression. Particularly relevant: Experience with serving frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM or llama.cpp. CUDA kernel work and multi-GPU communication with NCCL. Experience with inference runtimes such as ONNX Runtime, ExecuTorch or GGML. Why join? You'll join at an early stage and help shape the inference stack before it's set in stone. Research and inference sit close together, so your work affects how the models are built as well as how fast they run. There's real room to grow, with plenty to learn alongside strong researchers and engineers. Package & location Compensation: £150,000 - £200,000 + equity Location: London Working model: Hybrid, around three days a week in the office If you've optimised LLM serving or written GPU kernels for production models and want to work close to the research, we'd be interested in speaking with you. Contact Techire AI for a confidential conversation. All applicants will receive a response.

items.desc: Upfront wil de voedingsindustrie vereenvoudigen door de hele keten zelf in handen te nemen. We begonnen met ons eigen sportvoedingsmerk, openen nu onze Foodstores door heel Nederland en nemen straks ook de productie volledig in eigen handen. Alles bouwen we zelf, van onze producten en winkels tot de systemen erachter. Dat lukt alleen met de beste mensen in ieder vakgebied, die eigenaarschap nemen over wat ze maken. We zoeken een afstudeerstudent voor ons computer vision team. Het team werkt aan een automatische self-checkout voor onze Foodstores: camera’s zien welke producten een klant pakt, zodat afrekenen vanzelf gaat. Daarvoor moet het systeem klanten volgen, hun houding begrijpen en hun handelingen met producten herkennen. Binnen het team liggen een aantal onderzoeksvragen die dat systeem flink kunnen verbeteren, maar waar nu geen capaciteit voor is. Het zijn langlopende projecten met een onzekere uitkomst, dat maakt ze geschikt voor een afstudeeropdracht. Dit is geen meewerkstage. Het grootste deel van je tijd gaat naar onderzoek: bijvoorbeeld uitzoeken waarom een model iemand kwijtraakt als twee klanten voor hetzelfde schap staan. Daarna bouw je je methode echt, train je hem en meet je of hij op onze data beter presteert dan wat er nu draait. Mogelijke onderzoeksonderwerpen Continu tracken in drukte. Hoe volgen we klanten zonder onderbreking, ook als mensen dicht op elkaar staan of elkaar afschermen, zonder privacygevoelige kenmerken als gezicht, uiterlijk of lichaamsbouw? Realtime 3D pose estimation onder occlusie. Hoe voorspellen we een nauwkeurige 3D pose, ook als schappen of andere klanten het zicht blokkeren? Complexe handacties herkennen. Hoe identificeren we betrouwbaar handacties waarbij meerdere handelingen op meerdere producten plaatsvinden? Trainen op synthetische data uit de digitale winkel. Hoe simuleren we de winkel en het gedrag van klanten zo goed mogelijk, en hoe zetten we die data optimaal in om het systeem te trainen in plaats van echte opnames? Hogere labelkwaliteit. Hoe sporen we labelfouten automatisch op en corrigeren we ze, en hoe bepalen we welke samples het meeste opleveren om te laten labelen? Verantwoordelijkheden Breng de huidige staat van een deel van ons systeem in kaart. Onderzoek de state of the art binnen jouw onderwerp. Ontwikkel een eigen methode en implementeer die. Test je methode op ons systeem en vergelijk hem met de huidige aanpak. Schrijf je resultaten uit in een thesis of publicatie. Deel je bevindingen met het computer vision team, zodat zij erop verder kunnen bouwen. Wat je meebrengt Nieuwsgierigheid die blijft staan als een experiment niet werkt: onderzoek met een onzekere uitkomst geeft je energie. Zelfstandigheid om een onderzoeksvraag scherp te krijgen en zes maanden werk zelf te plannen. Je zit in de afstudeerfase van een technische master aan de TU Delft, zoals Computer Science, Robotics of Electrical Engineering. Ervaring met deep learning voor computer vision, in Python en een framework als PyTorch. Het is een sterke pré als je al hebt gewerkt met tracking, pose estimation, action recognition, synthetische data of active learning. Benefits Een stagevergoeding van €750 per maand. Een begeleider uit ons computer vision team, naast je begeleider vanuit de universiteit. Toegang tot ons systeem, onze data en de digitale winkel om je methode op te testen. Je werkt op onze Campus in de Van Nelle Fabriek in Rotterdam. Een open kantoor met veel licht en een grote tuin. Ontbijt, lunch en avondeten van onze eigen chefs met producten uit onze eigen winkel, elke dag vers gekookt. 20% personeelskorting en onbeperkt Upfront producten voor eigen gebruik. Een privé-gym en wellnessruimte met ijsbaden, sauna, douches en kleedkamers. Wekelijkse hyrox-lessen en runs met het team. En misschien wel het mooiste: de vrijheid. Je bepaalt zelf hoe je je werk aanpakt. Binnen jouw vakgebied ben jij de expert, en zo behandelen we je ook. We geven je graag de ruimte om je eigen ideeën te bedenken en implementeren.

items.title: Systems Performance Engineer, AI Infrastructure
items.card: You will build measurement tools and turn observations of real hardware and software into evidence for SIL’s simulation platform and the investment decisions it supports. Your work will range from targeted experiments on individual components to measurements of complete LLM serving systems. Working with workload, simulation and uncertainty specialists, you will investigate bottlenecks, explain performance variation
items.desc: About CommonAI CommonAI CIC is a non-profit organisation built around collaborative engineering and is backed by a mix of UK Government and private funding in order to design, build and deploy innovative AI systems. Our Scaling Inference Lab (SIL) is developing simulation grounded in real measurements to help the UK invest in promising AI infrastructure. We connect proposed hardware designs to realistic workloads, helping investors and engineers understand their potential, their limitations and the next experiment worth doing. The Opportunity Design and run experiments that reveal how AI infrastructure behaves, what limits its performance and how reliably that behaviour can be predicted. You will build measurement tools and turn observations of real hardware and software into evidence for SIL’s simulation platform and the investment decisions it supports. Your work will range from targeted experiments on individual components to measurements of complete LLM serving systems. Working with workload, simulation and uncertainty specialists, you will investigate bottlenecks, explain performance variation and identify the meaningful effects. We welcome deep expertise in one or more parts of the hardware and software stack. You will work with colleagues who bring complementary strengths, with scope to broaden your expertise as the team grows. What You Will Do Design and run reproducible experiments, from individual hardware or software components to complete LLM serving systems, covering relevant workloads, configurations and operating conditions. Develop reusable measurement tools and collect traces, profiles and counters to characterise latency, throughput, memory behaviour and, where reliable measurement is possible, power and energy. Investigate bottlenecks, performance variation and unexpected behaviour across the layers your expertise covers, working with colleagues to extend the investigation through the stack. Take responsibility for reproducible workload details, software versions, configuration and measurement methods so results can be reproduced, compared and used to calibrate simulator models. Work with simulation and uncertainty specialists to choose measurements that resolve important unknowns and undertake curation of calibration and validation data. Help define the controls needed for experiments and use the resulting cluster-control interfaces, coordinating access and changes with colleagues responsible for the hardware. An example early project would be to work with workload colleagues to establish a reproducible reference experiment and measurement dataset, investigating how performance changes under a selected configuration or load change. Requirements Experience investigating the performance of real computing systems and designing experiments that support rigorous conclusions. Depth in one or more relevant areas: accelerator profiling, inference runtimes, memory systems, distributed/HPC workloads, networking, or power and energy measurement. The ability to build maintainable automation and analysis tools in a suitable software language, and to learn unfamiliar profiling tools. Knowledge and care of experimental controls, repeatability, confounding effects and the limits of a measurement. Some experience using AI coding agents, alongside sound debugging and review habits. LLM serving experience and familiarity with tools such as Nsight, PyTorch Profiler or system/network profilers would be useful. These are examples, not a requirement to know every tool. Strong expertise in one part of the stack is welcome; we can shape the role and recruit complementary strengths around it. Why join us Help build UK AI capability and improve how investment and compute serve the public good. Build a network spanning UK hardware SMEs, major technology companies, venture and public investors, and leading universities. Shape a growing team with startup pace and close academic links. Use frontier models and coding agents with a substantial tooling budget. Benefits A collaborative and supportive work environment The opportunity to have a high impact in a growing organisation Competitive salary package, including pension and benefits Professional development opportunities Networking opportunities with influential figures from across the tech sector and academia A vibrant office environment located a few minutes’ walk away from Cambridge train station Salary range: £60,000 - £110,000 per annum Working with us Hybrid, with regular time in Cambridge agreed individually around hardware work and collaboration; applicants across the UK are welcome. We are open to permanent employment, part-time arrangements and consultancy. We would like you to start as soon as practical and can be flexible for the right person. We particularly welcome experienced engineers but will also consider earlier-career candidates with strong evidence of ability. Relevant postgraduate study is useful, but qualifications are secondary to experience …

items.title: Entry-Level AI Engineer
items.card: The role exists to support the engineering team in accelerating AI product developments, optimizing existing data pipelines, and integrating modern machine learning frameworks into scalable production systems. By joining our team, you will play a direct part in advancing innovative artificial intelligence technologies while growing your technical expertise in a supportive, collaborative environment. What you'll do
items.desc: Role Summary The Entry-Level AI Engineer position is a 6-month fixed-term role focused on building, testing, and deploying machine learning models and artificial intelligence solutions. The role exists to support the engineering team in accelerating AI product developments, optimizing existing data pipelines, and integrating modern machine learning frameworks into scalable production systems. By joining our team, you will play a direct part in advancing innovative artificial intelligence technologies while growing your technical expertise in a supportive, collaborative environment. What you'll do Design, train, and evaluate foundational machine learning and deep learning models under senior supervision. Clean, preprocess, and structure large datasets for training and testing pipelines. Implement data processing workflows using Python, Pandas, and NumPy. Collaborate with software engineers to integrate AI models into RESTful APIs and application backends. Conduct technical experiments, benchmark algorithm performance, and document findings. Participate in code reviews, testing procedures, and agile sprint planning sessions. Monitor model performance in production and assist in troubleshooting output anomalies. Explore emerging artificial intelligence tools, libraries, and frameworks to enhance internal engineering capabilities. What success looks like By month three, you will have successfully familiarized yourself with the internal data pipelines, actively contributed to dataset preprocessing, and collaborated with senior engineers on model experimentation. By month six, you will have independently trained and evaluated multiple machine learning models, contributed to RESTful API integrations, and actively participated in agile delivery cycles. What you'll bring Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a related quantitative discipline. Proficiency in Python programming and core software engineering concepts. Solid foundation in machine learning algorithms, statistical methods, and deep learning principles. Hands-on experience with frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Scikit-Learn through academic coursework, projects, or internships. Familiarity with version control tools including Git. Strong analytical problem-solving abilities and clear English communication skills. Nice to have Prior internship or project experience deploying machine learning models to production environments. Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure. Experience working within agile software development teams. How you'll work This is a hybrid role based in London, UK, combining collaborative office days with flexible remote working options. The position is offered on a 6-month fixed-term employment contract. Compensation & benefits This 6-month fixed-term role offers competitive compensation aligned with market standards. Additional professional development support and internal learning resources are available to help you build a strong foundation in artificial intelligence engineering. Hiring process The recruitment process begins with an initial application review, followed by an introductory chat with a member of the talent team. Shortlisted candidates will then complete a technical assessment and interview with senior engineering leadership before a final decision is made. Inclusion statement We are an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workplace for everyone. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of background and are happy to discuss reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process.

As our current Student Data Scientist is graduating soon, we’re looking for a student who keeps data flowing and reliable, turns it into clear analyses and figures, and enjoys building practical tools along the way. You’ll work in our new ErgoLab in central Copenhagen and report to our Clinical Evidence Manager, while being a part of our Marketing Team. What you'll do Keep data flowing from the ErgoLab and our studies. You'll collect, combine and check data from lab instruments, questionnaires and other sources, so every dataset is complete, traceable and correct. Develop our data pipeline and build small practical tools and apps that make data collection, checks and analysis faster. Analyse data and turn the results into clear charts and figures for white papers, commercial materials and peer-reviewed journals. Work with Product Management, Engineering and Marketing so our product information rests on solid data. Document data, code and methods so others can repeat your work. Later on, help set up EMG and motion-capture sensors in test runs with pilot participants. You'll likely succeed if you Are enrolled in a relevant bachelor's or master's programme (first year master's preferred), e.g. data science, statistics, (biomedical) engineering or a related field. Code in Python (or R) and are comfortable with statistics. Care about data integrity: you check, document and version your work. Make clear, publication-quality figures. Communicate clearly in English. Any Nordic language is a plus. Advantage: experience with Claude Code, especially designing and building practical apps. Bonus: experience with EMG, motion capture or signal processing, or knowledge of ergonomics or the musculoskeletal system. What we offer Real responsibility for the data behind our evidence, in a newly set-up lab. Your figures in white papers, commercial materials and scientific publications. Flexible hours that fit around your studies and exams. A social atmosphere in our office in central Copenhagen. Gym benefit and paid internet at home. Practical matters Hours: 15–20 a week, mainly on site in Copenhagen V. twice a week, with flexibility around exam periods Start: First or second week of January 2027. We hope you can stay at least 12 months. Salary: DKK 175 per hour for master's students and DKK 160 per hour for bachelor's students. You need to live in Denmark and have the right to work here. We can't offer visa sponsorship or relocation. The Recruitment Process We review applications and hold interviews on an ongoing basis. We expect to make an offer before Christmas. What to Expect in the Recruitment Process Screening: A short phone call with our HR Manager to clarify your motivation, your expectations and practical matters (15–20 minutes) Interview: With our HR Manager and Clinical Evidence Manager (60–80 minutes, at our office). We'll ask you to give a short presentation of one of your previous projects, such as a study or design project. By the end of the interview, you will have a chance to meet one of the team members. Reference check Job offer About Contour We are on a mission to make the world a healthier place to work. Headquartered in Copenhagen with 30 years in business, Contour designs and develops ergonomic workplace equipment. We invented the RollerMouse, and 9 out of 10 users report our products helped relieve their pain. Following our acquisition of Active Key, we combine ergonomic design with specialized hygienic peripherals. We are actively expanding our portfolio and commercial presence across Europe and North America. We are a team of around 110 people globally, large enough for international reach, yet small enough that your work is visible and makes a real difference across the business. All applications will be treated confidentially. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of their background and identity. items.desc:
Join our Team
 About this opportunity 
 Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) turns the mobile network into a sensor: the same radio that carries traffic can also detect and track objects such as drones. We are now taking ISAC from the lab out into the air and into the field, and we are looking for two engineers who want to own how it is tested and how the systems behind it are built and kept running.
You will be part of the team that runs ISAC testing in the Lund Test Network (LTN), our live over-the-air test network in Lund, and that builds and operates our ambulating ISAC systems: self-contained, mobile sensing units that we take to field sites and that are now being replicated for deployments together with partners around the world. When ISAC developers need to see how their features behave in the real world, or a partner needs their system up and running, you are the one who makes it happen.
You will work side by side with the ISAC developers, as part of the same team. There is no hand-over between "development" and "test": you are involved from the moment a feature takes shape, developers join you in the field, and what you find goes straight back into the next iteration. This seamless cooperation is what lets us go from idea to over-the-air result in days rather than months.
 What you will do 
 Testing 
 Take ownership of ISAC over-the-air testing in the Lund Test Network: keeping the test setup available, documented and ready to use.
 Handle test requests from ISAC developers, from understanding what they need to verify to planning and executing the test.
 Configure and operate test scenarios with stationary LTN radio nodes as well as moving systems, including drone flights and mobile setups.
 Take part in field measurement campaigns outside Lund.
 Collect and analyze measurement data, logs and traces, and work with developers to explain deviations and find defects.
 Field systems 
 Build, integrate and maintain the ambulating ISAC systems: hardware assembly, servers, power and communication cabling, and firmware updates.
 Help scale the systems from a handful of units to many, by making the build repeatable: build instructions, checklists and acceptance tests for every new unit.
 Maintain and run the test scheme that keeps the system firmware reliable from release to release.
 Operate the backend services our partners depend on, with a focus on stability, availability and monitoring.
 Support partners and internal collaborators who run the systems: troubleshooting, onboarding and adapting interfaces to their setups.
 Across both 
 Work as part of the development team: join planning, give early feedback on testability, and debug issues together with the developers.
 Develop and automate test and deployment tooling, so that tests and new systems become faster to set up, easier to repeat and easier to analyze.
 The skills you bring 
 MSc in Electrical Engineering, Engineering Physics, Computer Science or equivalent.
 Programming skills in Python, C, or C++
 Interest in radio, RF measurements and hands-on lab and field work.
 You enjoy building, cabling and getting a physical system to work.
 Comfortable with Linux and basic networking.
 Ownership: you take responsibility for a test environment, for the systems you build and for your own development.
 A positive, can-do attitude and enjoyment of working closely with developers and partners.
 Curiosity about new technology, including using AI to amplify your work.
 Meriting: 
 Experience with drones; an EU drone pilot certificate (A1/A3 or A2) is a plus.
 Pre-offer checks including references and relevant background screening will be conducted for final candidates. 
 Why join Ericsson? At Ericsson, you´ll have an outstanding opportunity. The chance to use your skills and imagination to push the boundaries of what´s possible. To build solutions never seen before to some of the world’s toughest problems. You´ll be challenged, but you won’t be alone. You´ll be joining a team of diverse innovators, all driven to go beyond the status quo to craft what comes next.

Define and run the change management strategy, including communication, training, documentation and user onboarding. Provide structured reporting to the Responsible AI Office, regulatory owner, governance bodies and senior stakeholders. Experience designing and improving business processes and workflows, covering the solution lifecycle from requirements to testing, deployment and adoption. Experience with Agile delivery and Product/Epic Ownership, including backlog management, collaboration with technical teams and delivery tracking. items.desc: Inventer l'usine de demain vous fascine ? Rejoignez DELMIA en tant qu'Expert Système de Production & Jumeau Numérique de l'Usine. Vous contribuerez à imaginer, prototyper et définir la nouvelle génération de solutions qui permettront à nos clients de définir, simuler et optimiser leur système de production, du premier concept jusqu'à la validation détaillée, avant même de le construire. Poste à pourvoir en CDI, basé à Vélizy-Villacoublay (78). Vos missions Au sein de l'équipe Portefeuille DELMIA, vous contribuez à la vision, à la stratégie et à la définition des solutions dédiées à la définition, la simulation et l'optimisation du système de production . Ces solutions s'appuient sur le jumeau numérique de l'usine. Ce jumeau évolue sur plusieurs niveaux de définition, d'une représentation logique de haut niveau (flux, capacités, enchaînements) jusqu'à une définition physique détaillée (géométrie, cinématique, comportement des équipements et de leur commande). Vous intervenez sur l'ensemble du périmètre : la définition des processus de fabrication et leur validation virtuelle en environnement atelier, la définition et la validation du système de production (lignes, cellules, postes, ressources), à chaque niveau de maturité du jumeau numérique, la simulation des flux et des équipements, du comportement logique jusqu'au comportement physique, l'optimisation du système de production : performance, capacité, implantation, utilisation des ressources, la mise en service virtuelle, l'exploration des nouvelles technologies d'intelligence artificielle, en particulier l' IA physique : robotique intelligente, jumeaux numériques servant à l'entraînement par simulation, agents autonomes en environnement industriel… Vous travaillez dans une démarche exploratoire, proche de la recherche. Vous investiguez, prototypez et démontrez la valeur, puis vous traduisez vos résultats en spécifications détaillées. Pour cela, vous collaborez étroitement avec les équipes de développement et de recherche, les responsables produit, les équipes Industrie et Qualité. Vous travaillez également avec des partenaires technologiques de pointe dans le domaine de l'IA. Tout cela s'inscrit dans la nouvelle génération de logiciels Dassault Systèmes, appelée Gen7. Chaque exploration s'appuie sur des enjeux métier et opérationnels concrets, pour que la valeur apportée soit tangible et différenciante. Explorer les technologies émergentes et en prouver la valeur , notamment l'IA physique. items.desc: Réf. de l'offre : AXAFR_2026100095 Localisation : NANTERRE - 92 Contrat : CDI Dispositifs handicap Société : AXA France Télétravail (selon profil poste) Expérience : Expérimentés Salaire : Selon profil et expérience VOTRE RÔLE ET VOS MISSIONS Vous souhaitez mettre votre expertise en data science au service d’enjeux concrets de tarification ? Vous avez envie de contribuer à la performance d’un acteur majeur de l’assurance auto ? Au sein de la Direction dédiée à l’IARD Particuliers , vous rejoignez l’équipe Pricing Technique, Affaire Nouvelle et Remplacement Auto . Vous intervenez au cœur de la tarification automobile , sur un marché très concurrentiel marqué par l’émergence des insurtech et assurtech. Avec 3 millions de contrats représentant près de 1,8 milliard d’euros de chiffre d’affaires auto , AXA est leader sur le marché de l’auto et continue d’innover pour répondre aux attentes de ses clients. L’équipe travaille sur le pricing commercial et le pricing technique des contrats auto. Votre objectif : mettre votre expertise en data science au service des études tarifaires et produire des analyses fiables et directement exploitables pour accompagner les actuaires et les équipes pricing. Vos missions En tant que Data scientist tarification IARD (F/H) , vos principales missions sont : Analyse et études tarifaires Répondre aux demandes des équipes pricing en réalisant les extractions, analyses et études tarifaires nécessaires ; Préparer les données utiles aux études et construire les variables pertinentes à partir d’un patrimoine de plus de 4 000 variables ; Analyser la fréquence et la sévérité des sinistres, les frais, l’ élasticité au prix , la durée de vie des contrats et la valeur client ; Modélisation et data science Appliquer, entraîner et comparer différents modèles : GLM, gradient boosting, réseaux de neurones et approches hybrides ; Tester et mesurer la performance des modèles afin de produire des analyses fiables et exploitables ; Étudier la sensibilité au prix, les comportements de la concurrence et les dynamiques du marché automobile ; Qualité, industrialisation et suivi Contrôler la qualité des données et contribuer à leur fiabilisation ; Développer principalement avec Python, PySpark et Spark , en veillant à la qualité et à la reproductibilité des traitements ; Accompagner la mise en production et le suivi des modèles en appliquant les pratiques de versioning, tests et MLOps ; Missions transverses Restituer vos analyses aux équipes pricing et aux interlocuteurs métier de manière claire et accessible ; Documenter et partager vos travaux, méthodes et bonnes pratiques ; Contribuer aux travaux transverses au sein du Groupe AXA, notamment avec Direct Assurances . VOTRE PROFIL Vous combinez expertise data , compréhension métier et goût du collectif. Compétences techniques et professionnelles recherchées: Maîtriser Python et PySpark , ainsi que les principales méthodes et bibliothèques de machine learning ; Analyser et modéliser des données avec rigueur, en garantissant la qualité, la reproductibilité et la documentation de vos travaux ; Comprendre les enjeux métier et restituer des résultats clairs et directement exploitables. Savoir-être Faire preuve de curiosité, rigueur et autonomie ; Communiquer avec pédagogie et savoir prendre du recul sur vos analyses ; Aimer travailler en équipe et partager vos connaissances. Vous êtes titulaire d’un Bac+5 en data science, informatique, statistiques, mathématiques appliquées ou équivalent et disposez d’au moins 3 ans d’expérience en data science . Une connaissance de la tarification est un plus. POURQUOI NOUS REJOINDRE ? Nous sommes persuadés que pour bien prendre soin de nos clients, nous devons commencer par bien prendre soin de nos collaborateurs ! Les avantages que nous proposons à nos salariés sont nombreux. Nous choisir, c’est bénéficier par exemple : D’un package de rémunération complet comprenant un salaire fixe, un complément de rémunération variable, des primes, de la participation et de l’intéressement, la possibilité d’acquérir des actions AXA, ou encore des solutions d’épargne avantageuses ; D’un cadre de travail flexible jusqu’à 3 jours de télétravail possible par semaine (selon profil du poste), des tickets restaurant pour les jours télétravaillés ou encore une participation à l’achat d’un écran ou fauteuil ergonomique ; D’une politique visant à concilier vie personnelle et vie professionnelle avec 28 jours de congés payés, entre 14 et 16 RTT selon les années, des formules de travail à temps partiel ou encore des jours d’absence rémunérées pour la rentrée scolaire ou un déménagement par exemple ; De la possibilité de s’engager pour une cause qui vous tient à cœur grâce à nos associations telles que AXA Atout Cœur, AXA Compétences Solidaires ou encore AXA Prévention ; Et bien plus encore ! Perspectives de développement des compétences et de carrières immenses, CE, conciergerie, offres privilèges, soutien en cas d’épreuve personnelle…On s’arrête …

items.desc: Sviluppo software, agenti AI, automazione e integrazione di sistemi Ottica Duemila ricerca una figura da inserire nel proprio team tecnologico con lo scopo di incrementare lo sviluppo di nuove soluzioni software e innovazione dei processi aziendali mediante l'utilizzo dell'intelligenza artificiale. Siamo alla ricerca di una persona curiosa, intraprendente, con una buona preparazione informatica e una forte predisposizione all'utilizzo delle nuove tecnologie AI applicate allo sviluppo software. Il candidato ideale dovrà essere in grado di utilizzare strumenti di intelligenza artificiale generativa e agenti AI per progettare, sviluppare e implementare nuove soluzioni tecnologiche, acquisendo progressivamente autonomia nella gestione dei progetti assegnati. Principali attività Progettazione e sviluppo di nuovi applicativi software attraverso l'utilizzo di strumenti e agenti AI. Sviluppo di integrazioni tra piattaforme, database, API e sistemi informatici aziendali. Creazione e implementazione di automazioni intelligenti. Sviluppo di strumenti interni per l'ottimizzazione dei processi aziendali. Progettazione e configurazione di agenti AI in grado di svolgere attività specifiche. Analisi delle esigenze aziendali e individuazione di soluzioni tecnologiche. Gestione dei progetti software, dalla progettazione al rilascio. Testing, debugging, manutenzione e documentazione delle soluzioni sviluppate. Ricerca e sperimentazione di nuove tecnologie. Requisiti richiesti Conoscenza dei principi fondamentali della programmazione. Conoscenza di uno o più linguaggi di programmazione, preferibilmente Python, PHP o JavaScript. Conoscenza di base di HTML, CSS, SQL e database relazionali. Familiarità con API REST, JSON e integrazioni tra sistemi. Capacità di utilizzare strumenti di intelligenza artificiale applicati alla programmazione. Predisposizione all'utilizzo di agenti AI e strumenti di sviluppo assistito dall'intelligenza artificiale. Capacità di analisi, ragionamento logico e problem solving. Capacità di organizzare il proprio lavoro e gestire progressivamente in autonomia i progetti assegnati. Interesse per l'innovazione tecnologica e l'apprendimento continuo. Costituiscono titolo preferenziale Esperienza con strumenti quali ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, Cursor, Claude Code o strumenti analoghi. Conoscenza di piattaforme di automazione come n8n o Make. Conoscenza dei sistemi Linux e degli ambienti server. Familiarità con Git e sistemi di controllo delle versioni. Conoscenza di piattaforme e-commerce. Esperienza nella creazione di agenti AI, workflow automatizzati e integrazioni con modelli linguistici (LLM). Realizzazione di progetti software personali, anche attraverso strumenti di sviluppo assistito dall'intelligenza artificiale. Chi stiamo cercando Non cerchiamo esclusivamente un programmatore tradizionale, ma una figura capace di sfruttare le potenzialità dell'intelligenza artificiale per trasformare idee ed esigenze aziendali in soluzioni software concrete, funzionali e affidabili. La capacità di apprendere rapidamente, sperimentare, risolvere problemi e sviluppare nuove soluzioni rappresenta un elemento fondamentale nella selezione.
